sentences.zh: 【晉紀四】起屠維作噩，盡著雍郭牂，凡十年。

translations.literal: 【Jin Annals 4】 Beginning in Tuxi Zuo'e, ending in Zhu Yong Guo Qiang, ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: 【Jin Annals 4】 From the year Tuxi Zuo'e through the year Zhu Yong Guo Qiang—ten years in all.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin, latter part of the Taikang era, tenth year (

translations.literal: jiyou, AD 289)

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，太廟成。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Grand Ancestral Temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Grand Ancestral Temple was completed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，祫祭。

translations.literal: On yisi, a joint ancestral sacrifice was held.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the court performed the joint ancestral rite.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆遣使請降，五月，詔拜廆鮮卑都督。

translations.literal: Murong Hui sent envoys to request submission; in the fifth month, an edict appointed Hui Xianbei Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui sent envoys to offer submission, and in the fifth month an edict appointed him Xianbei Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 廆謁見何龕，以士大夫禮，巾衣詣門；

translations.literal: Hui called on He Kan, using the rites due a scholar-official, wearing a headcloth and robes when he came to the gate;
translations.idiomatic: When Hui went to call on He Kan, he observed the courtesies owed a scholar-official, wearing a headcloth and civilian robes at the gate;

sentences.zh: 龕嚴兵以見之，廆乃改服戎衣而入。

translations.literal: Kan received him with troops drawn up in formation, so Hui changed into military dress before entering.
translations.idiomatic: Kan received him under arms in full array, so Hui changed into military dress before going in.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，廆曰：「主人不以禮待客，客何為哉！」

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Hui said, "The host does not treat his guest with courtesy—what is the guest to do!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Hui said, "When the host does not receive his guest with proper courtesy, what is the guest supposed to do!"

sentences.zh: 龕聞之，甚慚，深敬異之。

translations.literal: When Kan heard this, he was deeply ashamed and came to respect Hui greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan heard this, he was deeply ashamed and held Hui in still greater esteem.

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑宇文氏、段氏方強，數侵掠廆，廆卑辭厚幣以事之。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianbei Yuwen and Duan clans were powerful and repeatedly raided Hui; Hui addressed them with humble words and rich gifts to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xianbei Yuwen and Duan clans were at the height of their power and raided Hui again and again, so he placated them with humble words and lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 段國單于階以女妻廆，生皝、仁、昭。

translations.literal: Duan chieftain Jie gave his daughter to Hui in marriage, and she bore Huang, Ren, and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan chieftain Jie gave his daughter to Hui in marriage, and she bore Huang, Ren, and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 廆以遼東僻遠，徙居徒河之青山。

translations.literal: Because Liaodong was remote and isolated, Hui moved his seat to Green Mountain on the Tu River.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Liaodong too remote, Hui moved his seat to Green Mountain on the Tu River.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，復明堂及南郊五帝位。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Bright Hall and the positions of the Five Emperors at the southern suburb were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Bright Hall and the southern suburban altars to the Five Emperors were restored.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙辰，尚書令濟北成侯荀勖卒。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on bingchen, Minister of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Cheng of Jibei Xun Xu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Xun Xu, Minister of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Cheng of Jibei, died.

sentences.zh: 勖有才思，善伺人主意，以是能固其寵。

translations.literal: Xu was talented and thoughtful, skilled at discerning the ruler's intent, and so was able to secure his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was gifted and quick-witted, adept at reading the emperor's mind, and by that means he kept his favor secure.

sentences.zh: 久在中書，專管機事。

translations.literal: He had long served in the Secretariat and alone managed confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had long served in the Secretariat, where he alone handled confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 及遷尚書，甚罔悵。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to the Masters of Writing, he was deeply vexed and discontented.
translations.idiomatic: When he was moved to the Masters of Writing, he was deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 人有賀之者，勖曰：「奪我鳳皇池，諸君何賀邪！」

translations.literal: When someone congratulated him, Xu said, "You have robbed me of the Phoenix Pool—why do you congratulate me!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone congratulated him, Xu said, "You have taken away my Phoenix Pool—what is there to congratulate!"

sentences.zh: 帝極意聲色，遂至成疾。

translations.literal: The emperor indulged music and women to the utmost and thereby fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave himself over utterly to music and women and fell seriously ill as a result.

sentences.zh: 楊駿忌汝南王亮，排出之。

translations.literal: Yang Jun resented the Prince of Runan, Liang, and had him sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, who resented the Prince of Runan, Sima Liang, had him posted out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以亮為侍中、大司馬、假黃鉞、大都督、督豫州諸軍事，鎮許昌；

translations.literal: On jiashen, Liang was made Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, with the yellow battle-axe conferred, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and supervisor of all military affairs in Yuzhou, stationed at Xuchang;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Liang was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, with the yellow battle-axe conferred, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and supervisor of all military affairs in Yuzhou, with his headquarters at Xuchang;

sentences.zh: 徙南陽王柬為秦王，都督關中諸軍事；

translations.literal: the Prince of Nanyang, Jian, was moved to be Prince of Qin and made commander of all military affairs in Guanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Nanyang, Sima Jian, was reassigned as Prince of Qin and made commander of all military affairs in Guanzhong;

sentences.zh: 始平王瑋為楚王，都督荊州諸軍事；

translations.literal: the Prince of Shiping, Wei, was made Prince of Chu and commander of all military affairs in Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Shiping, Sima Wei, was made Prince of Chu and commander of all military affairs in Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 濮陽王允為淮南王，都督揚、江二州諸軍事；

translations.literal: the Prince of Puyang, Yun, was made Prince of Huainan and commander of all military affairs in Yang and Jiang provinces;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Puyang, Sima Yun, was made Prince of Huainan and commander of all military affairs in Yang and Jiang provinces;

sentences.zh: 並假節之國。

translations.literal: all were granted the ceremonial staff and sent to their fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: each was granted the ceremonial staff and sent to his domain.

sentences.zh: 立皇子乂為長沙王，穎為成都王，晏為吳王，熾為豫章王，演為代王，皇孫遹為廣陵王。

translations.literal: The emperor's sons Yi, Ying, Yan, Chi, and Yan were made princes of Changsha, Chengdu, Wu, Yuzhang, and Dai respectively, and the imperial grandson You was made Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's sons Yi, Ying, Yan, Chi, and Yan were enfeoffed as princes of Changsha, Chengdu, Wu, Yuzhang, and Dai, and the imperial grandson You as Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 又封淮南王子迪為漢王，楚王子儀為毘陵王，徙扶風王暢為順陽王，暢弟歆為新野公。

translations.literal: Further, the Prince of Huainan's son Di was enfeoffed as Prince of Han; the Prince of Chu's son Yi as Prince of Piling; the Prince of Fufeng, Chang, was moved to be Prince of Shunyang; and Chang's younger brother Xin was made Duke of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed the Prince of Huainan's son Di as Prince of Han, the Prince of Chu's son Yi as Prince of Piling, moved the Prince of Fufeng, Chang, to be Prince of Shunyang, and made Chang's younger brother Xin Duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 暢，駿之子也。

translations.literal: Chang was Yang Jun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Yang Jun's son.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王覲弟澹為東武公，繇為東安公。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye, Jing's younger brothers Dan and Yao were made Duke of Dongwu and Duke of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Langye's younger brothers Dan and Yao were made Duke of Dongwu and Duke of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 覲，人由之子也。

translations.literal: Jing was the son of Ren You.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was the son of Ren You.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以才人謝玖賜太子，生皇孫遹。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had given the talented lady Xie Jiu to the crown prince, and she bore the imperial grandson You.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had given the consort Xie Jiu to the crown prince, and she bore the imperial grandson You.

sentences.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，帝登樓望之，遹年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中曰：「暮夜倉猝，宜備非常，不可令照見人主。」

translations.literal: Once when a fire broke out in the palace at night, the emperor went up a tower to look; You, five years old, pulled the emperor's robe into the shadows and said, "In the haste of night one should guard against the unexpected—it must not be allowed that the ruler be seen in the light."
translations.idiomatic: Once when fire broke out in the palace at night, the emperor climbed a tower to watch; You, then five, pulled him by the robe into the shadows and said, "In the sudden confusion of night one must guard against the unexpected—the ruler must not be exposed to view."

sentences.zh: 帝由是奇之。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at this because of it.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the emperor regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 嘗對群臣稱遹似宣帝，故天下咸歸仰之。

translations.literal: He once told the assembled ministers that You resembled Emperor Xuan, and so all under Heaven looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his ministers that You resembled Emperor Xuan of Jin, and all under Heaven came to look to him with hope.

sentences.zh: 帝知太子不才，然恃遹明慧，故無廢立之心。

translations.literal: The emperor knew the crown prince lacked talent, yet relied on You's intelligence and brilliance, and therefore had no thought of deposing or replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew the crown prince was without talent, but trusted in You's brilliance, and so never considered removing him.

sentences.zh: 復用王佑之謀，以太子母弟柬、瑋、允分鎮要害。

translations.literal: He again adopted Wang You's plan, placing the crown prince's younger brothers by the same mother, Jian, Wei, and Yun, in command of strategic posts.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Wang You's counsel and posted the crown prince's uterine brothers Jian, Wei, and Yun to guard the key regions.

sentences.zh: 又恐楊氏之逼，復以佑為北軍中候，典禁兵。

translations.literal: Fearing pressure from the Yang clan, he again made You Central Commander of the Northern Army, in charge of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing coercion from the Yang clan, he again appointed You Central Commander of the Northern Army to hold the palace troops.

sentences.zh: 帝為皇孫遹高選僚佐，以散騎常侍劉寔志行清素，命為廣陵王傅。

translations.literal: For the imperial grandson You the emperor carefully chose aides; because Palace Attendant Liu Shi was known for pure conduct and integrity, he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: For the imperial grandson You the emperor chose his staff with great care; because Palace Attendant Liu Shi was known for integrity and plain living, he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 寔以時俗喜進趣，少廉讓，嘗著《崇讓論》，欲令初除官通謝章者，必推賢讓能，乃得通之。

translations.literal: Shi, because the age delighted in advancement and urgency and slighted modest yielding, once wrote 《On Honoring Yielding》, intending that anyone newly appointed who submitted a letter of thanks must first recommend and yield to the worthy and able before it could be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, seeing that men of the day loved advancement and scorned modest yielding, wrote 《On Honoring Yielding》, proposing that anyone newly appointed who submitted a letter of thanks must first recommend and yield to someone more worthy before the document could be accepted.

sentences.zh: 一官缺則擇為人所讓最多者用之，以為：「人情爭則欲毀己所不如，讓則競推於勝己。

translations.literal: When an office was vacant, the one most often yielded to by others was to be chosen; he held that "when human nature contends, men wish to destroy those they do not match; when they yield, they vie to push forward those who surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: When a post fell vacant, the man most often recommended by others in yielding was to be chosen. He argued, "When men contend, they seek to destroy those they cannot match; when they yield, they compete to advance those who surpass them.

sentences.zh: 故世爭則優劣難分，時讓則賢智顯出。

translations.literal: Therefore when the age contends, superior and inferior are hard to distinguish; when the time yields, the worthy and wise stand forth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in an age of contention, worth is hard to tell apart; in an age of yielding, the worthy and wise stand out plainly.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，能退身修己，則讓之者多矣，雖欲守貧賤，不可得也。

translations.literal: In such a time, those able to withdraw and cultivate themselves would be many who yielded, and even if one wished to remain in poverty and low station, it could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In such a time, those who could withdraw and cultivate themselves would be widely yielded to, and even if one wished to remain poor and obscure, one could not.

sentences.zh: 馳騖進趨而欲人見讓，猶卻行而求前也。」

translations.literal: To race in pursuit of advancement yet wish men to see one yielding is like stepping backward while seeking to go forward."
translations.idiomatic: To rush after advancement while wanting others to see you as yielding is like walking backward while trying to go forward."

sentences.zh: 淮南相劉頌上疏曰：「陛下以法禁寬縱，積之有素，未可一旦直繩御下，此誠時宜也。

translations.literal: Liu Song, administrator of Huainan, submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty, because legal prohibitions have been loose and indulgent and this has long been the practice, it is not possible all at once to apply the straight cord in governing subordinates—this is indeed timely.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song, administrator of Huainan, submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty, because the laws have long been lax and indulgent, it is not possible to govern your subjects all at once with the strictest rigor—that would indeed be timely counsel.

sentences.zh: 然至於矯世救弊，自宜漸就清肅；

translations.literal: Yet as for correcting the age and remedying abuses, one should naturally move gradually toward clarity and severity;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in correcting the age and remedying its abuses, you should move gradually toward clarity and discipline;

sentences.zh: 譬猶行舟，雖不橫截迅流，然當漸靡而往，稍向所趨，然後得濟也。

translations.literal: it is like traveling by boat: though one does not cut straight across the swift current, one should drift gradually onward, little by little turning toward one's goal, and only then can one cross.
translations.idiomatic: it is like steering a boat: though one does not cut straight across the swift current, one should ease gradually onward, inching toward one's goal, and only then reach the far shore.

sentences.zh: 自泰始以來，將三十年，凡諸事業，不茂既往，以陛下明聖，猶未反叔世之敝，以成始初之隆，傳之後世，不無慮乎！

translations.literal: From Taishi until now, nearly thirty years—of all undertakings none has flourished beyond what went before; with Your Majesty's brilliance and sagacity, you have still not reversed the abuses of a decadent age to achieve the splendor of the founding beginning—when this is handed down to later generations, will there not be cause for concern!
translations.idiomatic: From the Taishi era until now, nearly thirty years have passed, and in all undertakings none has surpassed what came before; with Your Majesty's brilliance, you have still not reversed the abuses of a decadent age to restore the splendor of the founding—should this not give posterity cause for concern!

sentences.zh: 使夫異時大業，或有不安，其憂責猶在陛下也。

translations.literal: If in another time the great enterprise should prove unstable, the burden of worry and blame will still rest on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If in days to come the great enterprise should falter, the burden of blame will still fall on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞為社稷計，莫若封建親賢。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in planning for the altars of soil and grain, nothing is better than enfeoffing kinsmen and the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in securing the altars of state, nothing avails more than enfeoffing kinsmen and the worthy.

sentences.zh: 然宜審量事勢，使諸侯率義而動者，其力足以維帶京邑；

translations.literal: Yet one should carefully weigh the situation, so that when feudatories act in accord with righteousness, their strength is sufficient to bind and protect the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you should weigh the situation carefully, so that when the feudal lords act in accord with duty, their strength is enough to shield the capital;

sentences.zh: 若包藏禍心者，其勢不足獨以有為。

translations.literal: if they harbor evil intent, their power is insufficient to act alone with effect.
translations.idiomatic: while those who harbor treacherous designs lack the power to act effectively on their own.

sentences.zh: 其齊此甚難，陛下宜與達古今之士，深共籌之。

translations.literal: To balance these is very difficult; Your Majesty should join with men versed in past and present and deliberate deeply together.
translations.idiomatic: To balance these is exceedingly hard; Your Majesty should consult deeply with men versed in past and present.

sentences.zh: 周之諸侯，有罪誅放其身，而國祚不泯；

translations.literal: Under Zhou, when feudal lords were guilty, they were executed or banished in person, yet their lineages were not extinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, when feudal lords sinned, they were executed or banished in person, yet their lines were not extinguished;

sentences.zh: 漢之諸侯，有罪或無子者，國隨以亡。

translations.literal: under Han, when feudal lords were guilty or had no sons, their states perished with them.
translations.idiomatic: under the Han, when feudal lords sinned or left no heirs, their states perished with them.

sentences.zh: 今宜反漢之敝，循周之舊，則下固而上安矣。

translations.literal: Now one should reverse Han's abuses and follow Zhou's old ways—then below would be secure and above at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now you should reverse the Han abuses and follow the Zhou precedent—then the realm below would be firm and the throne secure above.

sentences.zh: 天下至大，萬事至眾，人君至少，同於天日，是以聖王之化，執要於己，委務於下，非憚勞而好逸，誠以政體宜然也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is vast, the myriad affairs are numerous, and the ruler is the fewest—like the sun in the sky; therefore the sage king's transforming rule grasps essentials in himself and entrusts tasks to those below—not from fearing labor and loving ease, but truly because the body politic should be so.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven is vast, affairs are countless, and the ruler is but one—like the sun in the sky; therefore the sage king's rule holds the essentials himself and delegates the work below—not from fear of labor or love of ease, but because that is how government ought to be ordered.

sentences.zh: 夫居事始以別能否，甚難察也；

translations.literal: To judge ability and inability at the beginning of an undertaking is very hard to discern;
translations.idiomatic: To judge merit at the outset of an undertaking is very hard;

sentences.zh: 因成敗以分功罪，甚易識也。

translations.literal: to apportion merit and fault according to success and failure is very easy to recognize.
translations.idiomatic: to apportion merit and blame according to success and failure is very easy.

sentences.zh: 今陛下每精於造始而略於考終，此政功所以未善也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is each time exacting at the founding start and remiss at examining the end—this is why governmental achievement is not yet good.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is exacting at every beginning yet remiss at every end—that is why the government's achievements fall short.

sentences.zh: 人主誠能居易執要，考功罪於成敗之後，則群下無所逃其誅賞矣。

translations.literal: If the ruler can truly abide in what is easy and hold to essentials, examining merit and fault after success and failure, then those below have nowhere to escape his punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler can hold to essentials and judge merit and blame only after success or failure is known, then his ministers cannot escape reward or punishment.

sentences.zh: 古者六卿分職，塚宰為師；

translations.literal: In antiquity the six ministers divided duties, and the chief minister was their head;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the six ministers divided the duties of state, and the chief minister was their head;

sentences.zh: 秦、漢已來，九列執事，丞相都總。

translations.literal: from Qin and Han onward, the nine ranks held office and the chancellor gathered all under his command.
translations.idiomatic: from Qin and Han onward the nine ministers held office and the chancellor gathered all affairs under his command.

sentences.zh: 今尚書制斷，諸卿奉成，於古制為太重。

translations.literal: Now the Masters of Writing decide and cut off matters, and the various ministers merely carry out what is completed—compared with the ancient system this is too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Masters of Writing decide everything while the ministers merely execute—compared with antiquity, this concentrates too much power.

sentences.zh: 可出眾事付外寺，使得專之；

translations.literal: The multitude of affairs could be handed to the outer offices so that they might specialize in them;
translations.idiomatic: You could hand most affairs to the outer offices and let them specialize;

sentences.zh: 尚書統領大綱，若丞相之為，歲終課功，校簿賞罰而已，斯亦可矣。

translations.literal: the Masters of Writing would oversee the great outline, as the chancellor did, and at year's end examine achievement, check registers, and assign rewards and punishments—that would also suffice.
translations.idiomatic: the Masters of Writing would oversee the broad outline, as the chancellor once did, and at year's end examine achievement, check the registers, and assign rewards and punishments—that would suffice.

sentences.zh: 今動皆受成於上，上之所失，不得復以罪下，歲終事功不建，不知所責也。

translations.literal: Now in every motion they receive completed work from above; what the ruler above loses cannot again be charged to those below—when at year's end achievement is not established, one does not know whom to blame.
translations.idiomatic: Now every matter is decided above and merely executed below; the ruler's errors cannot be laid on his ministers—when year-end comes and nothing is accomplished, no one knows whom to blame.

sentences.zh: 夫細過謬妄，人情之所必有，而悉糾以法，則朝野無立人矣。

translations.literal: Small faults and mistaken absurdities are what human feeling must have, yet if all are prosecuted by law, then in court and country no one can stand.
translations.idiomatic: Petty faults are inevitable in human affairs, yet if all are prosecuted by law, then court and country alike will have no one left standing.

sentences.zh: 近世以來為監司者，類大綱不振而微過必舉，蓋由畏避豪強而又懼職事之曠，則謹密網以羅微罪，使奏劾相接，狀似盡公，而撓法在其中矣。

translations.literal: In recent generations those who served as overseers generally failed to raise the great outline yet were sure to bring up minute faults—largely because they feared and avoided the powerful while also fearing neglect of duty, and so drew tight nets to snare small crimes, making impeachments follow one after another, seeming wholly public-minded while bending the law lay within.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times overseers have failed to enforce the great principles yet seized on every petty fault—fearing the powerful while dreading neglect of duty, they weave tight nets for small crimes and file impeachment after impeachment, seeming wholly impartial while bending the law in the process.

sentences.zh: 是以聖王不善碎密之案，必責凶猾之奏，則害政之奸，自然禽矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage king does not favor fragmented, minute cases but must hold responsible vicious, crafty memorials—then the villains who harm government will naturally be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage king does not encourage fragmented, petty prosecutions but holds responsible vicious and crafty memorials—then the villains who harm government will be taken of themselves.

sentences.zh: 夫創業之勳，在於立教定制，使遺風系人心，餘烈匡幼弱，後世憑之，雖昏猶明，雖愚若智，乃足尚也。

translations.literal: The merit of founding an enterprise lies in establishing teaching and fixing institutions, so that surviving customs bind men's hearts and residual glory steadies the young and weak—later ages rely on these, and though dull they are still bright, though foolish as if wise—that is what is truly to be honored.
translations.idiomatic: The merit of founding a dynasty lies in establishing teaching and fixing institutions, so that surviving customs bind men's hearts and residual glory steadies the young and weak—later ages rely on these, and though dull they still shine, though foolish they still seem wise; that is what is truly worth honoring.

sentences.zh: 至夫修飾官署，凡諸作役，恆傷泰過，不患不舉，此將來所不須於陛下而自能者也。

translations.literal: As for adorning official halls and all sorts of labor service, they constantly harm by excess and extravagance, not by failing to be undertaken—this is what in the future Your Majesty need not provide and they will manage of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: As for adorning offices and all manner of public works, they constantly suffer from excess, not from neglect—future rulers will manage these without Your Majesty's needing to provide them.

sentences.zh: 今勤所不須以傷所憑，竊以為過矣。」

translations.literal: Now to be diligent in what is not needed and thereby harm what one relies upon—your servant privately considers this a fault."
translations.idiomatic: To labor at what is not needed and thereby harm what you rely upon—I venture to think that a fault."

sentences.zh: 帝皆不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could use none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted none of it.

sentences.zh: 詔以劉淵為匈奴北部都尉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Liu Yuan Northern Commander of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Liu Yuan Northern Commander of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 淵輕財好施，傾心接物，五部豪傑、幽冀名儒多往歸之。

translations.literal: Yuan was light with wealth and fond of giving, pouring out his heart in receiving others; heroes of the five tribes and famous scholars of You and Ji often went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was generous with wealth and open-handed, receiving others with wholehearted warmth; heroes of the five tribes and renowned scholars of You and Ji flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 奚軻男女十萬口來降。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand men and women of the Xi Ke came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thousand men and women of the Xi Ke submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝下永熙元年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu the Founder, first year of Yongxi (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin, latter part of the Yongxi era, first year (

sentences.zh: 庚戌，公元二九零年）

translations.literal: gengxu, AD 290)
translations.idiomatic: gengxu, AD 290)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉朔，改元太熙。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on xinyou the new moon, the era name was changed to Taixi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, xinyou, the era name was changed to Taixi.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以王渾為司徒。

translations.literal: On jisi, Wang Hun was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Wang Hun was appointed Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 司空、侍中、尚書令衛瓘子宣，尚繁昌公主。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Palace Attendant, and Minister of the Masters of Writing Wei Guan's son Xuan married the Princess of Fanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan, Minister of Works, Palace Attendant, and Minister of the Masters of Writing, had his son Xuan marry the Princess of Fanchang.

sentences.zh: 宣嗜酒，多過失，楊駿惡瓘，欲逐之，乃與黃門謀共毀宣，勸武帝奪公主。

translations.literal: Xuan was fond of wine and had many faults; Yang Jun hated Guan and wished to drive him out, so he plotted with the Yellow Gate to slander Xuan together and urged Emperor Wu to take back the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was given to drink and committed many faults; Yang Jun hated Guan and wished to drive him out, so he plotted with the Yellow Gate attendants to slander Xuan and urged Emperor Wu to take back the princess.

sentences.zh: 瓘慚懼，告老遜位。

translations.literal: Guan, ashamed and afraid, reported his age and yielded his post.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and afraid, Guan asked to retire on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 詔進瓘位太保，以公就第。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Guan to Grand Guardian and let him go to his mansion as a duke.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Guan to Grand Guardian and allowed him to retire to his mansion with ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 劇陽康子魏舒薨。

translations.literal: Wei Shu, Viscount Kang of Juyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu, Viscount Kang of Juyang, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲子，以右光祿大夫石鑒為司空。

translations.literal: Third month, on jiazi, Right Grand Master of Splendor Shi Jian was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiazi, Right Grand Master of Splendor Shi Jian was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝疾篤，未有顧命，勳舊之臣多已物故，侍中、車騎將軍楊駿獨侍疾禁中。

translations.literal: The emperor was gravely ill and had left no final charge; many meritorious old ministers had already passed away, and only Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun attended the illness within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gravely ill and had left no final instructions; most of the meritorious old ministers were already dead, and only Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun attended him within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 大臣皆不得在左右，駿因輒以私意改易要近，樹其心腹，會帝小間，見其新所用者，正色謂駿曰：「何得便爾！」

translations.literal: The great ministers were all unable to be at his side; Jun thereupon on his own authority changed and replaced those near at hand, planting his own trusted men. When the emperor had a slight respite and saw those newly appointed, he said sternly to Jun, "How dare you do this so readily!"
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers were kept from his side, and Jun on his own authority replaced those near the throne with his own men. When the emperor briefly rallied and saw the new appointments, he said sternly to Jun, "How dare you do this!"

sentences.zh: 時汝南王亮尚未發，乃令中書作詔，以亮與駿同輔政，又欲擇朝士有聞望者數人佐之。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Runan, Liang, had not yet set out, so he ordered the Secretariat to draft an edict appointing Liang and Jun to assist in government together, and also wished to choose several court gentlemen of reputation to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Runan, Liang, had not yet departed, so the emperor ordered the Secretariat to draft an edict appointing Liang and Jun as co-regents, and also wished to choose several reputable courtiers to assist them.

sentences.zh: 駿從中書借詔觀之，得便藏去，中書監華廙恐懼，自往索之，終不與。

translations.literal: Jun borrowed the edict from the Secretariat to look at it and, taking advantage of the moment, hid it away; Supervisor of the Secretariat Hua Yi was afraid and went in person to demand it, but in the end it was not given.
translations.idiomatic: Jun borrowed the edict from the Secretariat to read it and, seizing his chance, hid it away; Supervisor of the Secretariat Hua Yi went in person to demand it back, but Jun never returned it.

sentences.zh: 會帝復迷亂，皇后奏以駿輔政，帝頷之。

translations.literal: When the emperor again fell into confusion, the empress memorialized that Jun should assist in government, and the emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor relapsed into delirium, the empress submitted a memorial appointing Jun regent, and the emperor nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛丑，皇后召華廙及中書令何劭，口宣帝旨作詔，以駿為太尉、太子太傅、都督中外諸軍事、侍中、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on xinchou, the empress summoned Hua Yi and Secretariat Director He Shao, orally proclaimed the emperor's intent to draft an edict, and made Jun Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, commander of all military affairs within and without, Palace Attendant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on xinchou, the empress summoned Hua Yi and Secretariat Director He Shao, had them draft an edict in the emperor's name, and appointed Jun Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, commander of all military affairs within and without, Palace Attendant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 詔成，後對廙、邵以呈帝，帝視而無言。

translations.literal: When the edict was completed, the empress faced Yi and Shao and presented it to the emperor; the emperor looked at it and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was finished, the empress showed it to Yi and Shao and presented it to the emperor; he looked at it and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 廙，歆之孫；

translations.literal: Yi was the grandson of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the grandson of Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 劭，曾之子也。

translations.literal: Shao was Zeng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the son of He Zeng.

sentences.zh: 遂趣汝南王亮赴鎮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Runan, Liang, was urged to hurry to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The court then urged the Prince of Runan, Sima Liang, to depart for his post.

sentences.zh: 帝尋小間，問：「汝南王來未？」

translations.literal: The emperor soon had a slight respite and asked, "Has the Prince of Runan come yet?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon rallied slightly and asked, "Has the Prince of Runan arrived yet?"

sentences.zh: 左右言未至，帝遂困篤，己酉，崩於含章殿。

translations.literal: His attendants said he had not yet arrived; the emperor then fell into grave illness, and on jiyou he died in the Hall of Containing Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said he had not yet arrived; the emperor relapsed into grave illness, and on jiyou he died in the Hall of Containing Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 帝宇量弘厚，明達好謀，容納直言，未嘗失色於人。

translations.literal: The emperor's breadth of mind was great and generous, clear-sighted and fond of planning, receptive to blunt counsel, and he never showed loss of composure before others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was magnanimous and far-sighted, fond of deliberation, receptive to blunt counsel, and never lost his composure before others.

sentences.zh: 太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元，尊皇后曰皇太后，立妃賈氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name, honored the empress as empress dowager, and established Consort Jia as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name, honored the empress as empress dowager, and installed Consort Jia as empress.

sentences.zh: 楊駿入居太極殿，梓宮將殯，六宮出辭，而駿不下殿，以虎賁百人自衛。

translations.literal: Yang Jun entered and dwelt in the Hall of Supreme Pole; when the imperial coffin was about to be enshrined and the six palaces came out to take leave, Jun did not descend from the hall and guarded himself with a hundred tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun took up residence in the Hall of Supreme Pole; when the imperial coffin was about to be enshrined and the ladies of the six palaces came out to take leave, he refused to leave the hall and surrounded himself with a hundred tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 詔石鑒與中護軍張劭監作山陵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shi Jian and Central Commander of the Guard Zhang Shao to supervise construction of the mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shi Jian and Central Commander of the Guard Zhang Shao to supervise construction of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 汝南王亮畏駿，不敢臨喪，哭於大司馬門外。

translations.literal: The Prince of Runan, Liang, feared Jun and did not dare attend the mourning; he wept outside the Grand Marshal's gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Runan, Sima Liang, feared Yang Jun and did not dare attend the mourning rites, weeping instead outside the Grand Marshal's gate.

sentences.zh: 出營城外，表求過葬而行。

translations.literal: He went out and encamped outside the city, memorializing to request that he pass by the burial and then depart.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped outside the city walls and memorialized asking permission to pass by the burial before departing.

sentences.zh: 或告亮欲舉兵討駿者，駿大懼，白太后，令帝為手詔與石鑒、張劭，使帥陵兵討亮。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Liang intended to raise troops to attack Jun; Jun was greatly afraid, informed the empress dowager, and had the emperor write a personal edict to Shi Jian and Zhang Shao ordering them to lead the tomb guards to attack Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Liang intended to raise troops against him, Yang Jun was terrified; he informed the empress dowager and had the emperor write a personal edict to Shi Jian and Zhang Shao ordering them to lead the tomb guards against Liang.

sentences.zh: 劭，駿甥也，即帥所鄰趣鑒速發。

translations.literal: Shao was Jun's nephew by marriage and immediately led those near him to urge Jian to set out quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, Yang Jun's nephew by marriage, immediately led the troops at hand and urged Jian to march at once.

sentences.zh: 鑒以為不然，保持之。

translations.literal: Jian considered this wrong and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian judged this wrong and held Shao back.

sentences.zh: 亮問計於廷尉何勖，勖曰：「今朝野皆歸心於公，公不討人而畏人討邪！」

translations.literal: Liang asked Minister of Justice He Xu for counsel; Xu said, "Now court and country alike turn their hearts to you—will you not attack others yet fear others attacking you!"
translations.idiomatic: Liang asked Minister of Justice He Xu for advice; Xu said, "All the realm now looks to you—will you not strike first yet fear being struck yourself!"

sentences.zh: 亮不敢發，夜，馳赴許昌，乃得免。

translations.literal: Liang did not dare act; by night he galloped to Xuchang and only then escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Liang did not dare act; that night he galloped to Xuchang and so escaped.

sentences.zh: 駿弟濟及甥河南尹李斌皆勸駿留亮，駿不從。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Ji and his nephew by marriage, Administrator of Henan Li Bin, both urged Jun to keep Liang, but Jun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's younger brother Ji and his nephew by marriage, Administrator of Henan Li Bin, both urged him to keep Liang at court, but Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 濟謂尚書左丞傅咸曰：「家兄若征大司馬，退身避之，門戶庶幾可全。」

translations.literal: Ji said to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Xian, "If my elder brother campaigns against the Grand Marshal, let us withdraw and avoid him—then our house may perhaps be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Xian, "If my brother campaigns against the Grand Marshal, we should withdraw and keep clear—then our house may yet be preserved."

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「宗室外戚，相恃為安。

translations.literal: Xian said, "The imperial clan and the empress's kin rely on each other for safety.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The imperial clan and the empress's kin rely on each other for safety.

sentences.zh: 但召大司馬還，共崇至公以輔政，無為避也。」

translations.literal: Only summon the Grand Marshal back and together honor supreme fairness to assist in government—there is no need to avoid anything."
translations.idiomatic: Only summon the Grand Marshal back and together uphold the public good in governing—there is no need to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 濟又使侍中石崇見駿言之，駿不從。

translations.literal: Ji again had Palace Attendant Shi Chong see Jun and speak to him, but Jun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Ji again sent Palace Attendant Shi Chong to plead with Jun, but Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛未，葬武帝於峻陽陵。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on xinwei, Emperor Wu was buried at Junyang Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinwei, Emperor Wu was buried at Junyang Tomb.

sentences.zh: 楊駿自知素無美望，欲依魏明帝即位故事，普進封爵以求媚於眾。

translations.literal: Yang Jun knew he had never enjoyed a good reputation and wished to follow the precedent of Emperor Ming of Wei's accession, broadly advancing ranks and titles to win favor with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun knew he had never enjoyed a good reputation and wished to follow the precedent of Cao Rui's accession, broadly advancing ranks and titles to win the crowd's favor.

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍傅祗群臣皆增位一等，預喪事者增二等。

translations.literal: Left Army General Fu Zhi and all ministers were each raised one rank; those who took part in the mourning were raised two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army General Fu Zhi and all the ministers were each raised one rank; those who took part in the mourning were raised two.

sentences.zh: 二千石已上皆封關中侯，復租調一年。

translations.literal: All officials of two thousand piculs and above were enfeoffed as marquises within the passes, and land tax and corvée were remitted for one year.
translations.idiomatic: All officials of two thousand piculs and above were enfeoffed as marquises within the passes, and land tax and corvée were remitted for one year.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍石崇、散騎侍郎何攀共上奏，以為：「帝正位東宮二十餘年，今承大業，而班賞行爵，優於泰始革命之初及諸將平吳之功，輕重不稱。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Shi Chong and Palace Gentleman He Pan jointly submitted a memorial holding that "the emperor held the eastern palace for more than twenty years and now inherits the great enterprise, yet the distribution of rewards and bestowal of titles is more generous than at the beginning of the Taishi revolution and than the merit of the generals who pacified Wu—the weight does not match.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Shi Chong and Palace Gentleman He Pan jointly submitted a memorial arguing that "the emperor held the eastern palace for more than twenty years and now inherits the great enterprise, yet the distribution of rewards and titles is more generous than at the founding of the Taishi era or than the merit of the generals who pacified Wu—the scale does not match.

sentences.zh: 且大晉卜世無窮，今之開制，當垂於後，若有爵必進，則數世之後，莫非公侯矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Great Jin is divined to endure without end; the institutions opened now should be handed down to later ages—if every rank must advance, then after several generations none will not be dukes or marquises."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Great Jin is divined to endure forever; the institutions established now must be handed down—if every rank must advance, then within a few generations everyone will be a duke or marquis."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: This was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 詔以太尉駿為太傅、大都督、假黃鉞，錄朝政，百官總己以聽。

translations.literal: An edict made Grand Commandant Jun Grand Tutor, Grand Commander-in-Chief, with the yellow battle-axe conferred, recorder of court government, and all officials to gather affairs under himself and obey.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Grand Commandant Yang Jun Grand Tutor and Grand Commander-in-Chief, with the yellow battle-axe conferred, recorder of court government, with all officials to report to him.

sentences.zh: 傅咸謂駿曰：「諒闇不行久矣。

translations.literal: Fu Xian said to Jun, "Observance of mourning seclusion has long not been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian said to Jun, "Mourning seclusion has long gone unobserved.

sentences.zh: 今聖上謙沖，委政於公，而天下不以為善，懼明公未易當也。

translations.literal: Now the sage ruler is modest and yielding and entrusts government to you, yet all under Heaven do not regard this as good—I fear it will not be easy for you, sir, to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage ruler is modest and entrusts government to you, yet the realm does not regard this as good—I fear you will find the burden hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 周公大聖，猶致流言，況聖上春秋非成王之年乎！

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a great sage yet still drew slanderous talk—how much more when the sage ruler's years are not those of King Cheng of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou was a great sage yet still drew slander—how much more when the emperor is not yet of King Cheng's age!

sentences.zh: 竊謂山陵既畢，明公當審思進退之宜，苟有以察其忠款，言豈在多！」

translations.literal: Your servant privately holds that once the mountain tomb is finished, you, sir, should carefully consider what is fitting in advance and withdrawal—if there is means to perceive one's loyal sincerity, words need not be many!"
translations.idiomatic: I hold that once the tomb rites are finished, you should carefully consider whether to advance or withdraw—if loyalty can be seen, words need not be many!"

sentences.zh: 駿不從。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 咸數諫駿，駿漸不平，欲出咸為郡守。

translations.literal: Xian repeatedly admonished Jun; Jun gradually grew resentful and wished to send Xian out as a commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Xian repeatedly admonished Jun; Jun grew resentful and wished to post him out as a commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 李斌曰：「斥逐正人，將失人望。」

translations.literal: Li Bin said, "To drive out upright men will cause one to lose people's regard."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin said, "To drive out upright men will cost you the people's regard."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jun desisted.

sentences.zh: 楊濟遺咸書曰：「諺云：『生子癡，了官事。』

translations.literal: Yang Ji sent Xian a letter saying, "A proverb says, 'If you bear a foolish son, you finish official business.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji wrote to Xian, "A proverb says, 'Bear a foolish son and you finish official business.

sentences.zh: 官事未易了也。

translations.literal: Official business is not easy to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Official business is not so easily finished.

sentences.zh: 想慮破頭，故具有白。」

translations.literal: I have thought until my head might break—therefore I set this forth in full."
translations.idiomatic: I have thought until my head might split—therefore I set this forth in full."

sentences.zh: 咸復書曰：「衛公有言：『酒色殺人，甚於作直。』

translations.literal: Xian replied, "Master Wei said, 'Wine and women kill men—more than being upright does.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "Master Wei said, 'Wine and women kill a man—more than being upright does.

sentences.zh: 坐酒色死，人不為悔，而逆畏以直致禍，此由心不能正，欲以苟且為明哲耳。

translations.literal: To die from wine and women—men do not regret it, yet they perversely fear that uprightness brings disaster; this is because the heart cannot be straight and they wish to take expediency for wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Men do not regret dying from wine and women, yet they perversely fear that uprightness brings disaster—because their hearts are not straight and they mistake expediency for wisdom.

sentences.zh: 自古以直致禍者，當由矯枉過正，或不忠篤，欲以亢厲為聲，故致忿耳，安有悾悾忠益而返見怨疾乎！」

translations.literal: Since antiquity those who suffered disaster through uprightness did so because they bent the straight too far, or were not loyal and sincere, or wished to make a name by fierce severity—therefore they drew resentment; how could there be honest, loyal benefit yet in return meet hatred!"
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity those ruined by uprightness bent the straight too far, or were not loyal and sincere, or sought a reputation for fierce severity—hence resentment; how could honest loyalty meet hatred!"

sentences.zh: 楊駿以賈后險悍，多權略，忌之，故以其甥段廣為散騎常侍，管機密；

translations.literal: Yang Jun, because Empress Jia was dangerous, fierce, and full of stratagems, resented her; therefore he made his nephew by marriage Duan Guang Palace Attendant to manage confidential affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun resented Empress Jia for her fierce cunning and many stratagems, and therefore made his nephew by marriage Duan Guang Palace Attendant to manage confidential affairs;

sentences.zh: 張劭為中護軍，典禁兵。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao Central Commander of the Guard, in charge of the palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhang Shao Central Commander of the Guard to hold the palace troops.

sentences.zh: 凡有詔命，帝省訖，入呈太后，然後行之。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an edict or order, after the emperor reviewed it, it was presented to the empress dowager, and only then was it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was an edict, after the emperor reviewed it, it was presented to the empress dowager and only then enacted.

sentences.zh: 駿為政，嚴碎專愎，中外多惡之，馮翊太守孫楚謂駿曰：「公以外戚居伊、霍之任，當以至公、誠信、謙順處之。

translations.literal: Jun's governance was severe, minute, and willfully obstinate; within and without many hated him. Sun Chu, administrator of Fufeng, said to Jun, "You, sir, as an empress's kinsman hold the role of Yi Yin and Huo Guang—you should conduct yourself with supreme fairness, sincerity, and humble compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun governed with harsh pettiness and wilful obstinacy, and many within and without hated him. Sun Chu, administrator of Fufeng, said to him, "As an empress's kinsman you hold the role of Yi Yin and Huo Guang—you should govern with supreme fairness, sincerity, and humble compliance.

sentences.zh: 今宗室強盛，而公不與共參萬機，內懷猜忌，外樹私暱，禍至無日矣！」

translations.literal: Now the imperial house is powerful, yet you, sir, do not join them in deliberating on the myriad affairs, harbor suspicion within, and plant private favorites without—disaster will come any day!"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial house is powerful, yet you do not share in governing, harbor suspicion within, and favor your own partisans without—disaster will come any day!"

sentences.zh: 駿不從。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 楚，資之孫也。

translations.literal: Chu was Zi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was the grandson of Sun Zi.

sentences.zh: 弘訓少府蒯欽，駿之姑子也，數以直言犯駿，他人皆為之懼，欽曰：「楊文長雖暗，猶知人之無罪不可妄殺，不過疏我，我得疏，乃可以免；

translations.literal: Kuai Qin, Director of the Palace of Extended Instruction, was Jun's cousin by marriage; he repeatedly offended Jun with blunt speech, and others were all afraid for him. Qin said, "Yang Wenchang, though dull, still knows that a man without guilt must not be killed recklessly—at most he will distance me; if I am distanced, I can escape;
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Qin, Director of the Palace of Extended Instruction, was Yang Jun's cousin by marriage; he repeatedly offended Jun with blunt speech, and others feared for him. Qin said, "Yang Wenchang, though dull, still knows that the guiltless must not be killed recklessly—at most he will distance me, and distance will save me;

sentences.zh: 不然，與之俱族矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise, I shall be exterminated together with him."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I shall be exterminated with him."

sentences.zh: 駿辟匈奴東部人王彰為司馬，彰逃避不受。

translations.literal: Jun recruited Wang Zhang of the Eastern Xiongnu as Marshal; Zhang fled and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jun recruited Wang Zhang of the Eastern Xiongnu as Marshal; Zhang fled and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 其友新興張宣子怪而問之，彰曰：「自古一姓二后，未有不敗。

translations.literal: His friend Zhang Xuanzi of Xinxing, surprised, asked him; Zhang said, "Since antiquity, when one surname has had two empresses, there has never been failure to fall.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Zhang Xuanzi of Xinxing asked him in surprise; Zhang said, "Since antiquity, when one clan has produced two empresses, ruin has never failed to follow.

sentences.zh: 況楊太傅暱近小人，疏遠君子，專權自恣，敗無日矣。

translations.literal: How much more when Grand Tutor Yang draws near petty men, keeps distant from gentlemen, and monopolizes power at will—defeat is not a day away.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when Grand Tutor Yang favors petty men, keeps gentlemen at a distance, and monopolizes power at will—his fall is only a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 吾逾海出塞以避之，猶恐及禍，奈何應其辟乎！

translations.literal: I cross the sea and go beyond the frontier to avoid him—yet still fear reaching disaster; how could I answer his recruitment!
translations.idiomatic: I would cross the sea and go beyond the frontier to avoid him—yet still fear disaster; how could I accept his appointment!

sentences.zh: 且武帝不惟社稷大計，嗣子既不克負荷，受遺者復非其人，天下之亂可立待也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Emperor Wu did not consider the great plan of the altars of state; the heir could not bear the burden, and the one who received the testament was again not the right man—the chaos of all under Heaven can be awaited standing."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Emperor Wu did not consider the realm's great plan; the heir cannot bear the burden, and the one who received his testament is again not the right man—the chaos of the realm can be awaited standing."

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬午，立廣陵王遹為皇太子。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on renwu, the Prince of Guangling, You, was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on renwu, the Prince of Guangling, You, was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以中書監何劭為太子太師，衛尉裴楷為少師，吏部尚書王戎為太傅，前太常張華為少傅，衛將軍楊濟為太保，尚書和嶠為少保。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Secretariat He Shao was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Commandant of the Guards Pei Kai Junior Tutor; Minister of the Masters of Writing for Official Personnel Wang Rong Grand Mentor; former Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Hua Junior Mentor; General of the Guards Yang Ji Grand Guardian; and Master of Writing He Qiao Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao, Supervisor of the Secretariat, was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Pei Kai, Commandant of the Guards, Junior Tutor; Wang Rong, Minister of the Masters of Writing for Official Personnel, Grand Mentor; Zhang Hua, former Minister of Ceremonies, Junior Mentor; Yang Ji, General of the Guards, Grand Guardian; and He Qiao, Master of Writing, Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 拜太子母謝氏為淑媛。

translations.literal: The crown prince's mother, Lady Xie, was appointed Lady of Cultivated Grace.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's mother, Lady Xie, was appointed Lady of Cultivated Grace.

sentences.zh: 賈后常置謝氏於別室，不聽與太子相見。

translations.literal: Empress Jia often placed Lady Xie in a separate chamber and would not allow her to meet the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia often kept Lady Xie in a separate chamber and would not let her see the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，和嶠嘗從容言於武帝曰：「皇太子有淳古之風，而末世多偽，恐不了陛下家事。」

translations.literal: Earlier, He Qiao had once said at ease to Emperor Wu, "The crown prince has the manner of pure antiquity, yet a decadent age is full of falsity—I fear he will not manage Your Majesty's household affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, He Qiao had once said frankly to Emperor Wu, "The crown prince has the manner of pure antiquity, yet a decadent age is full of falsity—I fear he will not manage your household affairs."

sentences.zh: 武帝默然。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was silent.

sentences.zh: 後與荀勖等同侍武帝，武帝曰：「太子近入朝差長進，卿可俱詣之，粗及世事。」

translations.literal: Later, together with Xun Xu and others he attended Emperor Wu; the emperor said, "The crown prince has recently come to court and improved somewhat—you may all go to him together and roughly touch on affairs of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Later, attending Emperor Wu together with Xun Xu and others, the emperor said, "The crown prince has recently come to court and improved somewhat—you may all visit him together and touch on affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 既還，勖等並稱太子明識雅度，誠如明詔。

translations.literal: When they returned, Xu and the others all praised the crown prince's clear understanding and elegant bearing, truly as the enlightened edict said.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, Xu and the others all praised the crown prince's clear understanding and elegant bearing, just as the emperor had said.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「聖質如初。」

translations.literal: Qiao said, "His sage quality is as at first."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said, "His quality is as at first."

sentences.zh: 武帝不悅而起。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, displeased, rose and left.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, displeased, rose and left.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，嶠從太子遹入朝，賈后使帝問曰：「卿昔謂我不了家事，今日定如何？」

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Qiao followed the crown prince You into court; Empress Jia had the emperor ask, "You once said I could not manage household affairs—how is it today?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Qiao followed Crown Prince You into court; Empress Jia had the emperor ask, "You once said I could not manage household affairs—how about today?"

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「臣昔事先帝，曾有斯言；

translations.literal: Qiao said, "Your servant formerly served the late emperor and once had those words;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said, "I formerly served the late emperor and once said as much;

sentences.zh: 言之不效，國之福也。」

translations.literal: that the words did not prove true is the state's good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: that my words did not prove true is the state's good fortune."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛酉，以石鑒為太尉，隴西王泰為司空。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on xinyou, Shi Jian was made Grand Commandant and the Prince of Longxi, Tai, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on xinyou, Shi Jian was appointed Grand Commandant and the Prince of Longxi, Sima Tai, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以劉淵為建威將軍、匈奴五部大都督。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan was made General Who Establishes Might and Grand Commander of the Five Xiongnu Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Grand Commander of the Five Xiongnu Tribes.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, first year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, first year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元二九一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, AD 291)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, AD 291)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，改元永平。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on yiyou the new moon, the era name was changed to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, yiyou, the era name was changed to Yongping.

sentences.zh: 初，賈后之為太子妃也，嘗以妒，手殺數人，又以戟擲孕妾，子隨刃墮；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Jia was crown princess, she had once out of jealousy killed several people with her own hands, and also hurled a halberd at a pregnant concubine so that the child fell with the blade;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Empress Jia was crown princess, she had killed several people out of jealousy with her own hands, and once hurled a halberd at a pregnant concubine so that the child fell with the blade;

sentences.zh: 武帝大怒，修金墉城，將廢之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly enraged, repaired Jinyong City, and was about to depose her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was furious, repaired Jinyong City, and was about to depose her.

sentences.zh: 荀勖、馮紞、楊珧及充華趙粲共營救之，曰：「賈妃年少，妒者婦人常情，長自當差。」

translations.literal: Xun Xu, Feng Dan, Yang Wan, and Brilliant Companion Zhao Can jointly worked to rescue her, saying, "Consort Jia is young; jealousy is a woman's common feeling—when she grows older it will naturally improve."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu, Feng Dan, Yang Wan, and Brilliant Companion Zhao Can jointly pleaded for her, saying, "Consort Jia is young; jealousy is a woman's common feeling—she will improve with age."

sentences.zh: 楊后曰：「賈公閭有大勳於社稷，妃親其女，正復妒忌，豈可遽忘其先德邪！」

translations.literal: Empress Yang said, "Lord Jia of the state had great merit for the altars of state; the consort is his daughter—even if she is jealous, how can one abruptly forget her forebears' virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang said, "Lord Jia rendered great service to the state; the consort is his daughter—even if she is jealous, how can one forget her family's merit so soon!"

sentences.zh: 妃由是得不廢。

translations.literal: The consort thereby was not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was thereby spared deposition.

sentences.zh: 后數誡厲妃，妃不知后之助己，返以后為構己於武帝，更恨之。

translations.literal: The empress repeatedly admonished and urged the consort; the consort did not know the empress had helped her and instead took the empress as one who had framed her before Emperor Wu, hating her all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The empress repeatedly admonished the consort, who did not know the empress had helped her and instead believed the empress had framed her before Emperor Wu, hating her all the more.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，賈后不肯以婦道事太后，又欲干預政事，而為太傅駿所抑。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Empress Jia refused to serve the empress dowager in the way of a daughter-in-law and also wished to intervene in government, but was restrained by Grand Tutor Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Empress Jia refused to serve the empress dowager as a daughter-in-law should and wished to intervene in government, but was restrained by Grand Tutor Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 殿中中郎渤海孟觀、李肇，皆駿所不禮也，陰構駿，云將危社稷。

translations.literal: Central Gentleman of the Palace Meng Guan of Bohai and Li Zhao were both men whom Jun did not treat with courtesy; they secretly framed Jun, saying he would endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Central Gentleman of the Palace Meng Guan of Bohai and Li Zhao were both men whom Yang Jun had slighted; they secretly plotted against him, saying he would endanger the state.

sentences.zh: 黃門董猛，素給事東宮，為寺人監，賈后密使猛與觀、肇謀誅駿，廢太后。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Dong Meng had long served the eastern palace as eunuch supervisor; Empress Jia secretly had Meng plot with Guan and Zhao to execute Jun and depose the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Dong Meng had long served the eastern palace as eunuch supervisor; Empress Jia secretly had him plot with Guan and Zhao to kill Yang Jun and depose the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 又使肇報汝南王亮，使舉兵討駿，亮不可。

translations.literal: She also had Zhao inform the Prince of Runan, Liang, to raise troops to attack Jun; Liang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: She also had Zhao inform the Prince of Runan, Sima Liang, to raise troops against Yang Jun; Liang refused.

sentences.zh: 肇報都督荊州諸軍事楚王瑋，瑋欣然許之，乃求入朝。

translations.literal: Zhao informed the Prince of Chu, Wei, commander of all military affairs in Jingzhou; Wei gladly agreed and thereupon requested to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao informed the Prince of Chu, Sima Wei, commander of all military affairs in Jingzhou; Wei gladly agreed and requested permission to come to court.

sentences.zh: 駿素憚瑋勇銳，欲召之而未敢，因其求朝，遂聽之。

translations.literal: Jun had long feared Wei's courage and sharpness, wished to summon him yet did not dare; because he requested to attend court, Jun thereupon permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun had long feared Wei's courage and sharpness, wished to summon him yet did not dare; when Wei requested to attend court, Jun permitted it.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸酉，瑋及都督揚州諸軍事淮南王允來朝。

translations.literal: Second month, on guiyou, Wei and the Prince of Huainan, Yun, commander of all military affairs in Yangzhou, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guiyou, Wei and the Prince of Huainan, Sima Yun, commander of all military affairs in Yangzhou, came to court.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛卯，孟觀、李肇啟帝，夜作詔，誣駿謀反，中外戒嚴，遣使奉詔廢駿，以侯就第。

translations.literal: Third month, on xinmao, Meng Guan and Li Zhao reported to the emperor, drafted an edict by night, falsely charged Jun with plotting rebellion, put inner and outer quarters on alert, and sent envoys bearing the edict to depose Jun and send him to his mansion as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinmao, Meng Guan and Li Zhao reported to the emperor, drafted an edict by night falsely charging Yang Jun with rebellion, put the realm on alert, and sent envoys bearing the edict to depose him and send him to his mansion as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 命東安公繇帥殿中四百人討駿，楚王瑋屯司馬門，以淮南相劉頌為三公尚書，屯衛殿中，段廣跪言於帝曰：「楊駿孤公無子，豈有反理？

translations.literal: They ordered Duke of Dong'an Yao to lead four hundred men of the palace to attack Jun; the Prince of Chu, Wei, encamped at the Grand Marshal's gate; the Administrator of Huainan Liu Song was made Master of Writing for the Three Dukes and encamped to guard the palace; Duan Guang knelt and said to the emperor, "Yang Jun is isolated and without sons—how could there be logic in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: They ordered Duke of Dong'an Yao to lead four hundred palace guards against Yang Jun; the Prince of Chu, Wei, encamped at the Grand Marshal's gate; Liu Song, administrator of Huainan, was made Master of Writing for the Three Dukes and encamped to guard the palace; Duan Guang knelt before the emperor and said, "Yang Jun is isolated and without sons—how could he rebel?

sentences.zh: 願陛下審之！」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to examine this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine this carefully!"

sentences.zh: 帝不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not answer.

sentences.zh: 時駿居曹爽故府，在武庫南，聞內有變，召眾官議之。

translations.literal: At that time Jun dwelt in Cao Shuang's old mansion, south of the armory; hearing that there was trouble within, he summoned the assembled officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Jun dwelt in Cao Shuang's old mansion, south of the armory; hearing of trouble within, he summoned the officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 太傅主簿朱振說駿曰：「今內有變，其趣可知，必是閹豎為賈后設謀，不利於公。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor's Registrar Zhu Zhen urged Jun, saying, "Now there is trouble within—the direction can be known; it must be that eunuchs have plotted for Empress Jia, to your harm.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor's Registrar Zhu Zhen urged Yang Jun, saying, "There is trouble within—the direction is clear; eunuchs have plotted for Empress Jia, to your harm.

sentences.zh: 宜燒雲龍門以脅之，索造事者首，開萬春門，引東宮及外營兵擁皇太子入宮，取奸人，殿內震懼，必斬送之。

translations.literal: You should burn the Cloud Dragon Gate to intimidate them, demand the heads of those who made the plot, open the Gate of Ten Thousand Springs, lead the eastern palace and outer-camp troops to escort the crown prince into the palace, seize the villains—those within the hall will be terrified and will surely be beheaded and sent forth.
translations.idiomatic: You should burn the Cloud Dragon Gate to intimidate them, demand the heads of the plotters, open the Gate of Ten Thousand Springs, lead the eastern palace and outer-camp troops to escort the crown prince into the palace and seize the villains—those in the hall will be terrified and will surely be beheaded and sent forth.

sentences.zh: 不然，無以免難。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, there is no escaping disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise there is no escaping disaster."

sentences.zh: 駿素怯懦，不決，乃曰：「雲龍門，魏明帝所造，功費甚大，奈何燒之！」

translations.literal: Jun had always been timid and irresolute and said, "The Cloud Dragon Gate was built by Emperor Ming of Wei—the labor and expense were very great—how could we burn it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun had always been timid and irresolute and said, "The Cloud Dragon Gate was built by Emperor Ming of Wei at great labor and expense—how could we burn it!"

sentences.zh: 侍中傅祗白駿，請與尚書武茂入宮觀察事勢，因謂群僚曰：「宮中不宜空。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fu Zhi informed Jun, requesting to enter the palace with Master of Writing Wu Mao to observe how matters stood, and then said to the assembled officials, "The palace should not be left empty."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Fu Zhi reported to Yang Jun and asked to enter the palace with Master of Writing Wu Mao to assess the situation; he then told the assembled officials, "The palace must not be left empty."

sentences.zh: 遂揖而下階。

translations.literal: He then bowed and descended the steps.
translations.idiomatic: With that he bowed and went down the steps.

sentences.zh: 眾皆走，茂猶坐；

translations.literal: The crowd all fled, but Mao still sat;
translations.idiomatic: Everyone fled, but Wu Mao remained seated;

sentences.zh: 祗顧曰：「君非天子臣邪？

translations.literal: Zhi looked back and said, "Are you not a subject of the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi turned back and said, "Are you not a subject of the emperor?

sentences.zh: 今內外隔絕，不知國家所在，何得安坐！」

translations.literal: Now inner and outer are cut off—we do not know where the ruler is—how can you sit at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer courts are cut off, and we do not even know where the ruler is—how can you sit at ease!"

sentences.zh: 茂乃驚起。

translations.literal: Mao then startled and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao then startled and rose to his feet.

sentences.zh: 駿黨左軍將軍劉豫陳兵在門，遇右軍將軍裴頠，問太傅所在，頠紿之曰：「向於西掖門遇公乘素車，從二人西出矣。」

translations.literal: Jun's follower, General of the Left Army Liu Yu, arrayed troops at the gate; he encountered General of the Right Army Pei Kai and asked where the Grand Tutor was. Kai deceived him, saying, "A moment ago at the Western Side Gate I met the Lord riding a plain carriage with two attendants heading west."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's ally Liu Yu, General of the Left Army, arrayed troops at the gate; he encountered General of the Right Army Pei Kai and asked where the Grand Tutor was. Pei Kai deceived him, saying, "Moments ago at the Western Side Gate I met the Lord in a plain carriage with two attendants heading west."

sentences.zh: 豫曰：「吾何之？」

translations.literal: Yu said, "Where shall I go?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu said, "Where should I go?"

sentences.zh: 頠曰：「宜至廷尉。」

translations.literal: Kai said, "You should go to the Commandant of Justice."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai said, "You should report to the Commandant of Justice."

sentences.zh: 豫從頠言，遂委而去。

translations.literal: Yu followed Kai's words, then laid down his arms and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu took his advice, laid down his arms, and left.

sentences.zh: 尋詔頠代豫領左軍將軍，屯萬春門。

translations.literal: Soon an edict appointed Kai to replace Yu as General of the Left Army, encamped at Wanchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict appointed Pei Kai to replace Liu Yu as General of the Left Army, and he encamped at Wanchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 頠，秀之子也。

translations.literal: Kai was the son of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai was the son of Pei Xiu.

sentences.zh: 皇太后題帛為書，射之城外，曰：「救太傅者有賞。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wrote on silk and shot it outside the city wall, saying, "Whoever rescues the Grand Tutor will be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wrote a message on silk and shot it outside the city wall: "Whoever rescues the Grand Tutor will be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 賈后因宣言太后同反。

translations.literal: Empress Jia thereupon had it proclaimed that the Empress Dowager was likewise in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia then had it proclaimed that the Empress Dowager was likewise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尋而殿中兵出，燒駿府，又令弩士於閣上臨駿府而射之，駿兵皆不得出，駿逃於馬廄，就殺之。

translations.literal: Soon palace troops came out, burned Jun's mansion, and had crossbowmen on the tower overlook Jun's mansion and shoot at it. Jun's troops could not get out; Jun fled to the stables and there was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon palace troops emerged, burned Yang Jun's mansion, and had crossbowmen on the tower shoot down into it. Yang Jun's troops could not get out; he fled to the stables and was killed there.

sentences.zh: 孟觀等遂收駿弟珧、濟、張劭、李斌、段廣、劉豫、武茂及散騎常侍楊邈、中書令蔣俊、東夷校尉文鴦，皆夷三族，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Meng Guan and the others then seized Jun's younger brothers Yao and Ji, Zhang Shao, Li Bin, Duan Guang, Liu Yu, Wu Mao, and Attendant Cavalry-in-Ordinary Yang Miao, Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jun, and Commandant Protector of the Eastern Yi Wen Yang—all were exterminated to the third degree of kinship; those who died numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guan and the others then seized Yang Jun's younger brothers Yang Yao and Yang Ji, Zhang Shao, Li Bin, Duan Guang, Liu Yu, Wu Mao, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Miao, Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jun, and Eastern Yi Protector Wen Yang—all were exterminated to the third degree of kinship, and several thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 珧臨刑，告東安公繇曰：「表在石函，可問張華。」

translations.literal: As Yao faced execution, he told Duke of Dong'an Yao, "The memorial is in a stone casket—you can ask Zhang Hua."
translations.idiomatic: As Yang Yao faced execution, he told Duke of Dong'an Yao, "The memorial is in a stone casket—you can ask Zhang Hua."

sentences.zh: 眾謂宜依鐘毓例為之申理。

translations.literal: The crowd said one should, following the precedent of Zhong Yu, plead on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The others said one should plead his case following the precedent of Zhong Yu.

sentences.zh: 繇不聽，而賈氏族黨趣使行刑。

translations.literal: Yao would not listen, and the Jia clan faction hurried to have the execution carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao would not listen, and the Jia clan faction hurried to have the execution carried out.

sentences.zh: 珧號叫不已，刑者以刀破其頭。

translations.literal: Yao cried out unceasingly; the executioners broke his head with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao cried out without cease; the executioners split his head open with a blade.

sentences.zh: 繇，諸葛誕之外孫也，故忌文鴦，誣以為駿黨而誅之。

translations.literal: Yao was the maternal grandson of Zhuge Dan; therefore he resented Wen Yang and on false charges deemed him Jun's follower and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao was the maternal grandson of Zhuge Dan; he therefore resented Wen Yang and on false charges executed him as Yang Jun's follower.

sentences.zh: 是夜，誅賞皆自繇出，威振內外。

translations.literal: That night, rewards and punishments all issued from Yao; his authority shook inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: That night all executions and rewards issued from Sima Yao alone, and his authority shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 王戎謂繇曰：「大事之後，宜深遠權勢。」

translations.literal: Wang Rong said to Yao, "After a great affair, one ought to keep far from power."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong told Sima Yao, "After such a great affair, you ought to keep your distance from power."

sentences.zh: 繇不從。

translations.literal: Yao did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao did not listen.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On renchen, the realm was pardoned and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 賈后矯詔，使後軍將軍荀悝送太后於永寧宮，特全太后母高都君龐氏之命，聽就太后居。

translations.literal: Empress Jia forged an edict and had Rear Guards General Xun Kui escort the Empress Dowager to Yongning Palace; she specially spared the life of the Empress Dowager's mother, Lady Gao of Gaodu, allowing her to dwell with the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia forged an edict and had Rear Guards General Xun Kui escort the Empress Dowager to Yongning Palace; she specially spared the life of the Empress Dowager's mother, Lady Gao of Gaodu, and allowed her to live with the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 尋復諷群公有司奏曰：「皇太后陰漸奸謀，圖危社稷，飛箭系書，要募將士，同惡相濟，自絕於天。

translations.literal: Soon they again prompted the nobles and officials to memorialize, saying, "The Empress Dowager has secretly nurtured treacherous plots, seeking to endanger the altars of state; she shot arrows bearing messages and recruited soldiers—evildoers aiding one another, cutting herself off from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they again prompted the nobles and officials to memorialize, saying, "The Empress Dowager has secretly nurtured treacherous plots to endanger the state; she shot arrows bearing messages to recruit soldiers—evildoers aiding one another, cutting herself off from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 魯侯絕文姜，《春秋》所許。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Lu cast off Wen Jiang, the Spring and Autumn Annals approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Lu cast off Wen Jiang, the Spring and Autumn Annals approved.

sentences.zh: 蓋奉祖宗，任至公於天下，陛下雖懷無已之情，臣下不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: For we serve the royal ancestors and entrust utmost impartiality to the realm; though Your Majesty harbors boundless affection, your subjects dare not obey such an edict."
translations.idiomatic: We serve the royal ancestors and must entrust utmost impartiality to the realm; though Your Majesty harbors boundless affection, your subjects dare not obey such an edict."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此大事，更詳之。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "This is a grave matter—consider it further."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "This is a grave matter—examine it further."

sentences.zh: 有司又奉：「宜廢皇太后為峻陽庶人。」

translations.literal: The officials again presented: "The Empress Dowager should be deposed and made Commoner of Junyang."
translations.idiomatic: The officials again memorialized: "The Empress Dowager should be deposed and made Commoner of Junyang."

sentences.zh: 中書監張華議：「皇太后非得罪於先帝，今黨其所親，為不母於聖世，宜依漢廢趙太后為孝成后故事，貶皇太后之號，還稱武皇后，居異宮，以全始終之恩。」

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Zhang Hua argued: "The Empress Dowager did not offend the late emperor; now that her favorites have been destroyed, to treat her thus is unmotherly in an age of sage rule. One should follow the Han precedent of deposing Empress Zhao and restoring the title of Empress Xiaocheng—reduce her empress title, restore the style Empress Wu, and let her dwell in a separate palace, to preserve grace from first to last."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Zhang Hua argued: "The Empress Dowager did not offend the late emperor; now that her favorites have been destroyed, to treat her thus is unmotherly in an age of sage rule. One should follow the Han precedent of deposing Empress Zhao—reduce her empress title, restore the style Empress Wu, let her dwell in a separate palace, and thereby preserve grace from first to last."

sentences.zh: 左僕射荀愷與太子少師下邳王晃等議曰：「皇太后謀危社稷，不可復配先帝，宜貶尊號，廢詣金墉城。」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Xun Kai and Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Prince Huang of Xiapi, and others argued: "The Empress Dowager plotted to endanger the altars of state and cannot again be paired with the late emperor; her honored title should be reduced and she should be deposed and sent to Jincheng Fortress."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Xun Kai, Tutor of the Heir Apparent Prince Huang of Xiapi, and others argued: "The Empress Dowager plotted to endanger the state and cannot again be paired with the late emperor; her honored title should be reduced, and she should be deposed and sent to Jincheng Fortress."

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏請從晃等議，廢太后為庶人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials memorialized requesting that the opinion of Huang and the others be followed, deposing the Empress Dowager as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the officials memorialized to follow Prince Huang's opinion and deposed the Empress Dowager as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「楊駿造亂，家屬應誅，詔原其妻龐命，以尉太后之心。

translations.literal: They also memorialized: "Yang Jun raised disorder; his family should be executed; the edict spared the life of his wife, Lady Pang, to soothe the Empress Dowager's heart.
