translations.idiomatic: They also memorialized: "Yang Jun raised rebellion and his family should be executed; the edict had spared his wife Lady Pang to soothe the Empress Dowager's heart.

sentences.zh: 今太后廢為庶人，請以龐付廷尉行刑。」

translations.literal: Now that the Empress Dowager is deposed as a commoner, we request that Pang be handed to the Commandant of Justice for execution."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Empress Dowager has been deposed as a commoner, we request that Lady Pang be handed to the Commandant of Justice for execution."

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: The edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused.

sentences.zh: 有司復固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: The officials again pressed firmly, and only then was it granted.
translations.idiomatic: The officials pressed again, and at last it was granted.

sentences.zh: 龐臨刑，太后抱持號叫，截發稽顙，上表詣賈后稱妾，請全母命；

translations.literal: As Lady Pang faced execution, the Empress Dowager held her and cried out, cut off her hair and kowtowed, submitted a memorial to Empress Jia calling herself a concubine, and begged to spare her mother's life;
translations.idiomatic: As Lady Pang faced execution, the Empress Dowager held her and wailed, cut off her hair and kowtowed, submitted a memorial to Empress Jia in which she styled herself a concubine, and begged that her mother's life be spared;

sentences.zh: 不見省。

translations.literal: She was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: She received no heed.

sentences.zh: 董養游太學，升堂歎曰：「朝廷建斯堂，將以何為乎！

translations.literal: Dong Yang wandered in the Imperial Academy; mounting the hall he sighed and said, "The court built this hall—what was it meant for!
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yang wandered in the Imperial Academy; mounting the hall he sighed and said, "The court built this hall—what was it meant for!

sentences.zh: 每覽國家赦書，謀反大逆皆赦，至於殺祖父母、父母不赦者，以為王法所不容故也。

translations.literal: Whenever one reads the state's amnesty edicts, treason and great sedition are all pardoned; only killing one's grandparents and parents are not pardoned, because royal law cannot tolerate them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever one reads the state's amnesty edicts, treason and great sedition are all pardoned; only the killing of grandparents and parents is not pardoned, because the law cannot tolerate it.

sentences.zh: 奈何公卿處議，文飾禮典，乃至此乎！

translations.literal: How then can the nobles and ministers in council ornament ritual and statute to reach this point!
translations.idiomatic: Yet how can the nobles and ministers in council ornament ritual and statute to reach this point!

sentences.zh: 天人之理既滅，大亂將作矣。」

translations.literal: The principle of Heaven and humanity is already extinguished—great disorder is about to begin."
translations.idiomatic: The bond between Heaven and humanity is already broken—great disorder is about to erupt."

sentences.zh: 有司收駿官屬，欲悉誅之。

translations.literal: The officials seized Jun's staff and intended to execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: The officials seized Yang Jun's staff and intended to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 侍中傅祗啟曰：「昔魯芝為曹爽司馬，斬關赴爽，宣帝用為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fu Zhi submitted, saying, "In the past Lu Zhi was Cao Shuang's Chief of Staff, broke through the gates and went to Shuang; Emperor Xuan of Wei employed him as Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Fu Zhi submitted, saying, "In the past Lu Zhi served as Cao Shuang's chief of staff, broke through the gates and went to Shuang's aid; Emperor Xuan of Wei still employed him as inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 駿之僚佐，不可悉加罪。」

translations.literal: Jun's subordinates cannot all be heavily punished."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's subordinates cannot all be heavily punished."

sentences.zh: 詔赦之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，征汝南王亮為太宰，與太保衛瓘皆錄尚書事，輔政。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Prince of Runan, Liang, was summoned as Grand Preceptor; he and Grand Tutor Wei Guan were both put in charge of the Masters of Writing affairs and assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Prince Liang of Runan was summoned as Grand Preceptor; he and Grand Tutor Wei Guan were both placed in charge of Masters of Writing affairs to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 以秦王柬為大將軍，東平王楙為撫軍大將軍，楚王瑋為衛將軍、領北軍中候，下邳王晃為尚書令，東安公繇為尚書左僕射，進爵為王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Jian, was made Great General; the Prince of Dongping, Mao, was made General Who Pacifies the Army; the Prince of Chu, Wei, was made Defender General and acting Commander of the Northern Army; the Prince of Xiapi, Huang, was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Duke of Dong'an Yao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Qin was made Great General; Prince Mao of Dongping was made General Who Pacifies the Army; Prince Wei of Chu was made Defender General and acting commander of the Northern Army; Prince Huang of Xiapi was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Duke of Dong'an Yao was made left vice director of the Masters of Writing and advanced to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 楙，望之子也。

translations.literal: Mao was the son of Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mao was the son of Sima Wang.

sentences.zh: 封董猛為武安侯，三兄皆為亭侯。

translations.literal: Dong Meng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an; his three elder brothers were all made village marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Meng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an; his three elder brothers were all made village marquises.

sentences.zh: 亮欲取悅眾心，論誅楊駿之功，督將侯者千八十一人。

translations.literal: Liang wished to please the people's hearts; reckoning the merit of executing Yang Jun, they ennobled generals, commanders, and marquises—1,081 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang wished to win popular favor; reckoning the merit of executing Yang Jun, they ennobled generals, commanders, and marquises—1,081 persons in all.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞傅咸遺亮書曰：「今封賞熏赫，震動天地，自古以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Accounts Fu Xian sent Liang a letter saying, "Today's enfeoffments and rewards blaze conspicuously and shake Heaven and Earth—from antiquity until now, nothing like it has existed.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Accounts Fu Xian wrote to Prince Liang, saying, "Today's enfeoffments and rewards blaze conspicuously and shake Heaven and Earth—from antiquity until now, nothing like it has existed.

sentences.zh: 無功而獲厚賞，則人莫不樂國之有禍，是禍原無窮也。

translations.literal: Those who obtain lavish rewards without merit—then no one fails to rejoice when the state suffers disaster; the source of disaster is thus inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: If men obtain lavish rewards without merit, none will fail to rejoice when the state suffers disaster—the source of calamity is thus inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 凡作此者，由東安公。

translations.literal: All who did this came from the Duke of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: This was all the work of Duke of Dong'an Yao.

sentences.zh: 人謂殿下既至，當有以正之，正之以道，眾亦何怒！

translations.literal: People said that once Your Highness arrived, there ought to be correction; correct by the Way, and how would the crowd be angry!
translations.idiomatic: People said that once Your Highness arrived, matters would be set right; set them right by proper means, and how could the crowd be angry!

sentences.zh: 眾之所怒者，在於不平耳；

translations.literal: What the crowd is angry about is simply unfairness;
translations.idiomatic: What the crowd resents is simply unfairness;

sentences.zh: 而今皆更倍論，莫不失望。」

translations.literal: yet now all are rewarded at double reckoning—none fail to be disappointed."
translations.idiomatic: yet now all are rewarded at double reckoning—everyone is disappointed."

sentences.zh: 亮頗專權勢，咸復諫曰：「楊駿有震主之威，委任親戚，此天下所以喧嘩。

translations.literal: Liang was rather monopolistic in power; Xian again remonstrated, saying, "Yang Jun had an awing-the-ruler authority and entrusted power to kin—that is why the realm was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang was rather monopolistic in power; Fu Xian remonstrated again, saying, "Yang Jun awed the ruler and entrusted power to his kin—that is why the realm was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 今之處重，宜反此失，靜默頤神，有大得失，乃維持之，自非大事，一皆抑遣。

translations.literal: In holding heavy office now, you ought to reverse this error, remain quiet and nourish the spirit, intervene only in great gain or loss, and suppress and defer all else that is not a major affair.
translations.idiomatic: In holding high office now, you ought to reverse this error—remain quiet, nourish your spirit, intervene only in grave matters, and defer all else.

sentences.zh: 比過尊門，冠蓋車馬，填塞街衢，此之翕習，既宜弭息。

translations.literal: Lately when passing your honored gate, caps and canopies and carriages and horses fill the streets and lanes—this sort of eager throng ought already to be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Lately when passing your gate, caps and canopies and carriages and horses fill the streets—this eager thronging ought already to cease.

sentences.zh: 又夏侯長容無功而暴擢為少府，論者謂長容，公之姻家，故至於此；

translations.literal: Moreover Xiahou Changrong was abruptly promoted to Minister of the Palace Revenues though he had no merit; discussers say Changrong is Your Lordship's affinal kin, and therefore it reached this point;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xiahou Changrong was abruptly promoted to Minister of the Palace Revenues though he had no merit; observers say Changrong is Your Lordship's affinal kin, and that is why it happened;

sentences.zh: 流聞四方，非所以為益也。」

translations.literal: it spreads and is heard in all four directions—not a way to bring benefit."
translations.idiomatic: word spreads in all directions—not a way to bring benefit."

sentences.zh: 亮皆不從。

translations.literal: Liang would not heed any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang heeded none of it.

sentences.zh: 賈后族兄車騎司馬模、從舅右衛將軍郭彰、女弟之子賈謐與楚王瑋、東安王繇，並預國政。

translations.literal: Empress Jia's clan elder, Cavalry Commander-in-Ordinary Mo; her maternal uncle, Right Guard General Guo Zhang; and her younger sister's son Jia Mi, together with the Prince of Chu Wei and Prince of Dong'an Yao, all participated in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia's clan elder Sima Mo, Cavalry Commander-in-Ordinary; her maternal uncle Guo Zhang, Right Guard General; and her younger sister's son Jia Mi, together with Prince Wei of Chu and Prince Yao of Dong'an, all participated in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 賈后暴戾日甚，繇密謀廢后，賈氏憚之。

translations.literal: Empress Jia grew daily more cruel and violent; Yao secretly plotted to depose the empress, and the Jia clan feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia grew daily more cruel and violent; Sima Yao secretly plotted to depose her, and the Jia clan feared him.

sentences.zh: 繇兄東武公澹，素惡繇，屢譖之於太宰亮曰：「繇專行誅賞，欲擅朝政。」

translations.literal: Yao's elder brother, Duke of Dongwu Tan, had always hated Yao and repeatedly slandered him to Grand Preceptor Liang, saying, "Yao alone carries out rewards and punishments, seeking to monopolize court governance."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao's elder brother, Duke of Dongwu Tan, had always hated him and repeatedly slandered him to Grand Preceptor Prince Liang, saying, "Yao alone carries out rewards and punishments and seeks to monopolize court governance."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔免繇官；

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict dismissed Yao from office;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, an edict dismissed Sima Yao from office;

sentences.zh: 又坐有悖言，廢徙帶方。

translations.literal: also because of seditious words, he was deposed and banished to Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: also because of seditious words, he was deposed and banished to Daifang.

sentences.zh: 於是賈謐、郭彰權勢愈盛，賓客盈門。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jia Mi and Guo Zhang grew ever greater in power and influence; guests filled their gates.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jia Mi and Guo Zhang grew ever greater in power and influence, and clients filled their gates.

sentences.zh: 謐雖驕奢而好學，喜延士大夫。

translations.literal: Though Mi was arrogant and extravagant, he loved learning and delighted in receiving scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jia Mi was arrogant and extravagant, he loved learning and delighted in gathering scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 郭彰、石崇、陸機、機弟雲、和郁及滎陽潘岳、清河崔基、勃海歐陽建、蘭陵繆征、京兆杜斌、摯虞、琅邪諸葛詮、弘農王粹、襄城杜育、南陽鄒捷、齊國左思、沛國劉瑰、周恢、安平牽秀、穎川陳□□、高陽許猛、彭城劉訥、中山劉輿、輿弟琨，皆附於謐，號曰二十四友。

translations.literal: Guo Zhang, Shi Chong, Lu Ji, Ji's younger brother Yun, and He Yu, as well as Pan Yue of Xingyang, Cui Ji of Qinghe, Ouyang Jian of Bohai, Miao Zheng of Lanling, Du Bin of Jingzhao, Zhi Yu, Zhuge Quan of Langye, Wang Cui of Hongnong, Du Yu of Xiangcheng, Zou Jie of Nanyang, Zuo Si of Qi, Liu Gui of Pei, Zhou Hui, Qian Xiu of Anping, Chen [name lost] of Yingchuan, Xu Meng of Gaoyang, Liu Ne of Pengcheng, Liu Yu of Zhongshan, and Yu's younger brother Kun—all attached themselves to Mi and were called the Twenty-four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhang, Shi Chong, Lu Ji, Lu Yun, He Yu, Pan Yue of Xingyang, Cui Ji of Qinghe, Ouyang Jian of Bohai, Miao Zheng of Lanling, Du Bin of Jingzhao, Zhi Yu, Zhuge Quan of Langye, Wang Cui of Hongnong, Du Yu of Xiangcheng, Zou Jie of Nanyang, Zuo Si of Qi, Liu Gui of Pei, Zhou Hui, Qian Xiu of Anping, Chen [name lost] of Yingchuan, Xu Meng of Gaoyang, Liu Ne of Pengcheng, Liu Yu of Zhongshan, and Liu Kun—all attached themselves to Jia Mi and were called the Twenty-four Friends.

sentences.zh: 郁，嶠之弟也。

translations.literal: Yu was the younger brother of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He Yu was the younger brother of He Qiao.

sentences.zh: 崇與岳尤諂事謐，每候謐及廣城君郭槐出，皆降車路左，望塵而拜。

translations.literal: Chong and Yue were especially servile toward Mi; whenever they awaited Mi or Lady Guo of Guangcheng—Guo Huai—going out, they all descended from their carriages to the left side of the road and bowed to the dust.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong and Pan Yue were especially servile toward Jia Mi; whenever they awaited Jia Mi or Lady Guo of Guangcheng, Guo Huai, going out, they descended from their carriages to the left side of the road and bowed in the dust.

sentences.zh: 太宰亮、太保瓘以楚王瑋剛愎好殺，惡之，欲奪其兵權，以臨海侯裴楷代瑋為北軍中候。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Liang and Grand Tutor Guan, because the Prince of Chu Wei was obstinate and violent and loved killing, hated him and wished to strip him of military authority, using Marquis of Linhai Pei Kai to replace Wei as Commander of the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince Liang and Grand Tutor Wei Guan hated Prince Wei of Chu for his obstinacy and love of killing and wished to strip him of military authority, appointing Marquis of Linhai Pei Kai to replace him as commander of the Northern Army.

sentences.zh: 瑋怒；

translations.literal: Wei was enraged;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei was enraged;

sentences.zh: 楷聞之，不敢拜。

translations.literal: Kai heard of it and did not dare accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai heard of it and did not dare accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 亮復與瓘謀，遣瑋與諸王之國，瑋益忿怨。

translations.literal: Liang again plotted with Guan to send Wei with the princes to their fiefs; Wei grew still more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang again plotted with Wei Guan to send Prince Wei to his fief with the other princes; Prince Wei grew still more resentful.

sentences.zh: 瑋長史公孫宏、舍人岐盛，皆有寵於瑋，勸瑋自暱於賈后；

translations.literal: Wei's Chief Clerk Gongsun Hong and Attendant Qi Sheng were both favored by Wei and urged Wei to draw close to Empress Jia himself;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei's chief clerk Gongsun Hong and attendant Qi Sheng were both favored by him and urged him to draw close to Empress Jia;

sentences.zh: 后留瑋領太子太傅，盛素善於楊駿，衛瓘惡其反覆，將收之。

translations.literal: the Empress kept Wei as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Sheng had long been on good terms with Yang Jun—Wei Guan hated his fickleness and was about to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress kept Prince Wei on as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Qi Sheng had long been on good terms with Yang Jun—Wei Guan hated his fickleness and was about to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 盛乃與宏謀，因積弩將軍李肇矯稱瑋命，譖亮、瓘於賈后，云將謀廢立。

translations.literal: Sheng then plotted with Hong and, through Repeated-Bow General Li Zhao, falsely claimed Wei's orders and slandered Liang and Guan to Empress Jia, saying they were plotting deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Sheng then plotted with Gongsun Hong and, through Repeated-Bow General Li Zhao, falsely claimed Prince Wei's orders and slandered Prince Liang and Wei Guan to Empress Jia, saying they plotted to depose and install.

sentences.zh: 后素怨瓘，且患二公執政，己不得專恣；

translations.literal: The Empress had long resented Guan, and moreover feared the two lords holding power—she herself could not act arbitrarily;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia had long resented Wei Guan, and moreover feared the two lords holding power and preventing her from acting arbitrarily;

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，后使帝作手詔賜瑋曰：「太宰、太保欲為伊、霍之事，王宜宣詔，令淮南、長沙、成都王屯諸宮門，免亮及瓘官。」

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: the Empress had the emperor write an edict by hand and bestow it on Wei, saying, "The Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor wish to act as Yi Yin and Huo Guang did; the Prince ought to proclaim the edict, order the Princes of Huainan, Changsha, and Chengdu to encamp at the palace gates, and dismiss Liang and Guan from office."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, Empress Jia had the emperor write an edict by hand and bestow it on Prince Wei: "The Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor wish to act as Yi Yin and Huo Guang did; you should proclaim the edict, order the princes of Huainan, Changsha, and Chengdu to encamp at the palace gates, and dismiss Prince Liang and Wei Guan from office."

sentences.zh: 夜，使黃門繼以授瑋。

translations.literal: By night she had a Yellow Gate attendant follow and hand it to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: By night she had a palace attendant follow and deliver it to Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 瑋欲覆奏，黃門曰：「事恐漏洩，非密詔本意也。」

translations.literal: Wei wished to memorialize in reply; the Yellow Gate attendant said, "The affair fears leakage—this is not the intent of the secret edict."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei wished to memorialize in reply; the palace attendant said, "The affair may leak—this is not the intent of the secret edict."

sentences.zh: 瑋亦欲因此復私怨，遂勒本軍，復矯詔召三十六軍，告以「二公潛圖不軌，吾今受詔都督中外諸軍，諸在直衛者，皆嚴加警備；

translations.literal: Wei also wished thereby to settle private grievances; he thereupon mobilized his own army and again forged an edict summoning the Thirty-six Armies, announcing that "the two lords secretly plot irregular conduct; I now receive the edict to command all armies within and without; all on active palace guard duty must strictly increase vigil;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei also wished thereby to settle private grievances; he mobilized his own army and again forged an edict summoning the Thirty-six Armies, announcing that "the two lords secretly plot treason; I now receive the edict to command all armies within and without; all on active palace guard duty must increase vigilance;

sentences.zh: 其在外營，便相帥徑詣行府，助順討逆。」

translations.literal: those in outer camps should at once lead one another straight to the field headquarters to aid the legitimate and punish rebels."
translations.idiomatic: those in outer camps should at once lead one another straight to the field headquarters to aid the legitimate and punish rebels."

sentences.zh: 又矯詔「亮、瓘官屬，一無所問，皆罷遣之；

translations.literal: He also forged an edict: "Liang's and Guan's staff shall none be questioned—all are dismissed and sent away;
translations.idiomatic: He also forged an edict: "The staff of Prince Liang and Wei Guan shall none be questioned—all are dismissed and sent away;

sentences.zh: 若不奉詔，便軍法從事。」

translations.literal: if they do not obey the edict, let martial law be applied."
translations.idiomatic: if they do not obey the edict, martial law will be applied."

sentences.zh: 遣公孫宏、李肇以兵圍亮府，侍中、清河王遐收瓘。

translations.literal: He dispatched Gongsun Hong and Li Zhao with troops to surround Liang's mansion; Palace Attendant, Prince Xie of Qinghe, seized Guan.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Gongsun Hong and Li Zhao with troops to surround Prince Liang's mansion; Palace Attendant Prince Xie of Qinghe seized Wei Guan.

sentences.zh: 亮帳下督李龍，白「外有變，請拒之」，亮不聽。

translations.literal: Liang's Chief of Guards Li Long reported, "There is trouble outside—please resist it"; Liang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang's chief of guards Li Long reported, "There is trouble outside—please resist it"; Prince Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵登牆大呼，亮驚曰：「吾無貳心，何故至此！

translations.literal: Soon troops climbed the wall and shouted; Liang in alarm said, "I have no second heart—why have you come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Soon troops climbed the wall and shouted; Prince Liang said in alarm, "I have no second heart—why have you come to this!

sentences.zh: 詔書其可見乎？」

translations.literal: Can the edict be shown?"
translations.idiomatic: Can the edict be shown?"

sentences.zh: 宏等不許，趣兵攻之。

translations.literal: Hong and the others would not permit it and urged the troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong and the others refused and urged the troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 長史劉准謂亮曰：「觀此必是奸謀。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Liu Zhun said to Liang, "Judging from this, it must be a treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Liu Zhun said to Prince Liang, "Judging from this, it must be a treacherous plot.

sentences.zh: 府中俊乂如林，猶可力戰。」

translations.literal: Within the mansion, talented officers are thick as a forest—we can still fight with full strength."
translations.idiomatic: Within the mansion, talented officers are thick as a forest—we can still fight with full strength."

sentences.zh: 又不聽。

translations.literal: He again would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang again would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂為肇所執，歎曰：「我之赤心，可破示天下也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he was seized by Zhao and sighed, saying, "My loyal heart may be cut open and shown to all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince Liang was seized by Li Zhao and sighed, saying, "My loyal heart may be cut open and shown to all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 與世子矩俱死。

translations.literal: He died together with the heir Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He died together with his heir Ju.

sentences.zh: 衛瓘左右亦疑遐矯詔，請拒之，須自表得報，就戮未晚，瓘不聽。

translations.literal: Wei Guan's attendants also suspected that Xie had forged the edict and asked to resist; one need only memorialize and wait for a reply—there would be time enough to accept execution later. Guan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan's attendants also suspected that Prince Xie of Qinghe had forged the edict and asked to resist; they said one need only memorialize and wait for a reply—there would still be time to accept execution later. Guan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 初，瓘為司空，帳下督榮晦有罪，斥遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guan was Minister of Works, his Chief of Guards Rong Hui had committed an offense and was dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wei Guan served as Minister of Works, his chief of guards Rong Hui had committed an offense and was dismissed and sent away.

sentences.zh: 至是，晦從遐收瓘，輒殺瓘及子孫共九人，遐不能禁。

translations.literal: At this time, Hui followed Xie in seizing Guan and at once killed Guan and his descendants—nine persons in all; Xie could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Rong Hui followed Prince Xie in seizing Wei Guan and at once killed Guan and his descendants—nine persons in all; Prince Xie could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 岐盛說瑋「宜因兵勢，遂誅賈、郭，以正王室，安天下。」

translations.literal: Qi Sheng urged Wei, "You ought to take advantage of the army's momentum and thereupon execute Jia and Guo, to rectify the royal house and settle all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Sheng urged Prince Wei, "You ought to take advantage of the army's momentum and thereupon execute the Jia and Guo factions, to rectify the royal house and settle all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 瑋猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Wei hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 會天明，太子少傅張華使董猛說賈后曰：「楚王既誅二公，則天下威權盡歸之矣，人主何以自安！

translations.literal: When daybreak came, the Heir Apparent's Junior Tutor Zhang Hua sent Dong Meng to tell Empress Jia, "Now that the Prince of Chu has executed the two lords, all authority and power under Heaven will fall entirely to him—how can the sovereign secure himself!
translations.idiomatic: When daybreak came, the Heir Apparent's Junior Tutor Zhang Hua sent Dong Meng to tell Empress Jia, "Now that the Prince of Chu has executed the two lords, all authority and power under Heaven will fall entirely to him—how can the sovereign secure himself!

sentences.zh: 宜以瑋專殺之罪誅之。」

translations.literal: He ought to be executed on the charge of Wei's unauthorized killing."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei ought to be executed on the charge of unauthorized killing."

sentences.zh: 賈后亦欲因此除瑋，深然之。

translations.literal: Empress Jia also wished thereby to remove Wei and deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia also wished thereby to remove Prince Wei and deeply approved.

sentences.zh: 是時內外擾亂，朝廷恟懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: At this time, inside and outside were in turmoil; the court was terrified and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, inside and outside the capital were in turmoil; the court was terrified and knew not what to do.

sentences.zh: 張華白帝，遣殿中將軍王宮繼騶虞幡出麾眾曰：「楚王矯詔，勿聽也！」

translations.literal: Zhang Hua informed the emperor and sent Palace Guard General Wang Gong to follow with the Zouyu banner and command the masses, saying, "The Prince of Chu forged the edict—do not obey it!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua informed the emperor and sent Palace Guard General Wang Gong to follow with the Zouyu banner and command the troops, saying, "The Prince of Chu forged the edict—do not obey it!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆釋仗而走。

translations.literal: All released their weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: All released their weapons and fled.

sentences.zh: 瑋左右無復一人，窘迫不知所為，遂執之，下廷尉。

translations.literal: Wei had not a single attendant left; distressed and knowing not what to do, he was seized and turned over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei had not a single attendant left; distressed and knowing not what to do, he was seized and turned over to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，斬之。

translations.literal: On yichou, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 瑋出懷中青紙詔，流涕以示監刑尚書劉頌曰：「幸托體先帝，而受枉乃如此乎！」

translations.literal: Wei took from his bosom the edict written on blue paper, wept, and showed it to Supervising Execution Attendant-in-Chief Liu Song, saying, "Fortunate to owe my very body to the late emperor—and yet to suffer injustice to this degree!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei took from his bosom the edict written on blue paper, wept, and showed it to Supervising Execution Attendant-in-Chief Liu Song, saying, "Fortunate to owe my very body to the late emperor—and yet to suffer injustice to this degree!"

sentences.zh: 公孫宏、岐盛並夷三族。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong and Qi Sheng were both exterminated to the third degree of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong and Qi Sheng were both exterminated to the third degree of kinship.

sentences.zh: 瑋之起兵也，隴西王泰嚴兵將助瑋，祭酒丁綏諫曰：「公為宰相，不可輕動。

translations.literal: When Wei raised troops, Prince Tai of Longxi mustered his army and was about to aid Wei; Libationer Ding Sui remonstrated, saying, "My lord holds the office of chief minister—you must not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei raised troops, Prince Tai of Longxi mustered his army and was about to aid him; Libationer Ding Sui remonstrated, saying, "My lord holds the office of chief minister—you must not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 且夜中倉猝，宜遣人參審定問。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in the dead of night and in haste, you ought to send someone to investigate and verify the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the dead of night and in haste, you ought to send someone to investigate and verify the matter."

sentences.zh: 泰乃止。

translations.literal: Tai thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tai thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 衛瓘女與國臣書曰：「先公名謚未顯，每怪一國蔑然無言。

translations.literal: Wei Guan's daughter wrote to the state's ministers, saying, "My late father's name and posthumous title have not yet been made clear; I have always wondered that the whole realm stays utterly silent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan's daughter wrote to the state's ministers, saying, "My late father's name and posthumous title have not yet been made clear; I have always wondered that the whole realm stays utterly silent.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之失，其咎安在？」

translations.literal: Where lies the fault—the blame the Spring and Autumn Annals would assign?"
translations.idiomatic: Where then does the blame lie—the kind of wrong the Spring and Autumn Annals exists to record?"

sentences.zh: 於是太保主簿劉繇等執黃幡，撾登聞鼓，上言曰：「初，矯詔者至，公即奉送章綬，單車從命。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Tutor Chief Clerk Liu Yao and others took up the yellow banner, struck the Palace Appeal Drum, and submitted a memorial saying, "At first, when the forger of the edict arrived, my lord at once surrendered his seal and cord and went alone in a carriage to obey the command.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Grand Tutor Chief Clerk Liu Yao and others took up the yellow banner, struck the Palace Appeal Drum, and submitted a memorial saying, "At first, when the forger of the edict arrived, my lord at once surrendered his seal and cord and went alone in a carriage to obey the command.

sentences.zh: 如矯詔之文唯免公官，而故給使榮晦，輒收公父子及孫，一時斬戮。

translations.literal: Yet if the forged edict's text only dismissed my lord from office, whereas former attendant Rong Hui at once seized my lord, his sons, and his grandsons and executed them all at once—
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the forged edict's text only dismissed my lord from office, whereas former attendant Rong Hui at once seized my lord, his sons, and his grandsons and executed them all at once—

sentences.zh: 乞驗盡情偽，加以明刑。」

translations.literal: we beg that the truth and falsehood be fully examined and clear punishment be applied."
translations.idiomatic: we beg that the truth and falsehood be fully examined and clear punishment be applied."

sentences.zh: 乃詔族誅榮晦，追復亮爵位，謚曰文成。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued exterminating Rong Hui's clan to the third degree, restoring Liang's noble rank, and conferring the posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued exterminating Rong Hui's clan to the third degree, restoring Prince Liang's noble rank, and conferring the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 封瓘為蘭陵郡公，謚曰成。

translations.literal: Guan was enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan was enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 於是賈后專朝，委任親黨，以賈模為散騎常侍，加侍中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Empress Jia monopolized the court and entrusted office to her kin and partisans, appointing Jia Mo Regular Palace Attendant and adding Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Empress Jia monopolized the court and entrusted office to her kin and partisans, appointing Jia Mo Regular Palace Attendant and adding Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 賈謐與后謀，以張華庶姓，無逼上之嫌，而儒雅有籌略，為眾望所依，欲委以朝政。

translations.literal: Jia Mi plotted with the Empress: Zhang Hua was of common surname with no suspicion of pressing upon the sovereign; he was refined and cultured with strategy and planning, and was relied upon by public expectation—they wished to entrust him with court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi plotted with the Empress: Zhang Hua was of common surname with no suspicion of pressing upon the sovereign; he was refined and cultured with strategy and planning, and was relied upon by public expectation—they wished to entrust him with court affairs.

sentences.zh: 疑未決，以問裴頠贊成之。

translations.literal: Still undecided in their doubts, they asked Pei Ji, who approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Still undecided in their doubts, they asked Pei Ji, who approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 乃以華為侍中、中書監，頠為侍中，又以安南將軍裴楷為中書令，加侍中，與右僕射王戎並管機要。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua was then made Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; Pei Ji was made Palace Attendant; An'nan General Pei Kai was also made Secretary Supervisor and added Palace Attendant; together with Right Vice Director Wang Rong they jointly managed crucial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was then made Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; Pei Ji was made Palace Attendant; An'nan General Pei Kai was also made Secretary Supervisor and added Palace Attendant; together with Right Vice Director Wang Rong they jointly managed crucial affairs.

sentences.zh: 華盡忠帝室，彌縫遣闕，賈后雖凶險，猶知敬重華；

translations.literal: Hua was wholly loyal to the imperial house and patched omissions and gaps; although Empress Jia was fierce and dangerous, she still knew to respect Hua;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was wholly loyal to the imperial house and patched omissions and gaps; although Empress Jia was fierce and dangerous, she still knew to respect him;

sentences.zh: 賈模與華、頠同心輔政，故數年之間，雖暗主在上，而朝野安靜，華等之功也。

translations.literal: Jia Mo worked with Hua and Pei Ji in concert to assist governance; therefore within several years, though a dim sovereign sat above, court and countryside were tranquil—the achievement of Hua and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo worked with Zhang Hua and Pei Ji in concert to assist governance; therefore within several years, though a dim sovereign sat above, court and countryside were tranquil—the achievement of Hua and the others.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，分荊、揚十郡為江州。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: ten commanderies of Jing and Yang were separated off as Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, ten commanderies of Jing and Yang were separated off as Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛未，立隴西王泰世子越為東海王。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on xinwei, Prince Tai of Longxi's heir Yue was established as Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinwei, Prince Tai of Longxi's heir Yue was established as Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲午，秦獻王柬薨。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jiawu, Prince Xian of Qin, Jian, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Prince Xian of Qin, Jian, died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，征征西大將軍梁王肜為衛將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Grand General Conquering the West Prince Rong of Liang was summoned as Guard General and Recorder of Affairs for the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Grand General Conquering the West Prince Rong of Liang was summoned as Guard General and Recorder of Affairs for the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, second year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, second year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 壬子，公元二九二年）

translations.literal: renzi, AD 292)
translations.idiomatic: renzi, AD 292)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，己酉，故楊太后卒於金墉城。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, on jiyou, the former Empress Dowager Yang died at Jinyong City.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on jiyou, the former Empress Dowager Yang died at Jinyong City.

sentences.zh: 是時，太后尚有侍御十餘人，賈后悉奪之，絕膳八日而卒。

translations.literal: At this time the Empress Dowager still had more than ten attendants and ladies-in-waiting; Empress Jia seized them all; she went without food for eight days and died.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Empress Dowager still had more than ten attendants and ladies-in-waiting; Empress Jia seized them all; she went without food for eight days and died.

sentences.zh: 賈后恐太后有靈，或訴冤於先帝，乃覆而殯之，仍施諸厭劾符書、藥物等。

translations.literal: Empress Jia feared the Empress Dowager's spirit might plead her grievance before the late emperor; she therefore placed her face-down for burial and further applied various charm-talisman scripts and drugs of exorcism and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia feared the Empress Dowager's spirit might plead her grievance before the late emperor; she therefore placed her face-down for burial and further applied various charm-talisman scripts and drugs of exorcism and restraint.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬子，赦天下。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on renzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on renzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, third year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, third year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 癸丑，公元二九三年）

translations.literal: guichou, AD 293)
translations.idiomatic: guichou, AD 293)

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，弘農雨雹，深三尺。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: hail fell in Hongnong, three feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, hail fell in Hongnong, three feet deep.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑宇文莫槐為其下所殺，弟普撥立。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Yuwen chieftain Mohuai was killed by his subordinates; his younger brother Pobo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chieftain Yuwen Mohuai was killed by his subordinates; his younger brother Pobo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 拓跋綽卒，弟子弗立。

translations.literal: Tuoba Chuo died; his younger brother's son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Chuo died; his younger brother's son Fu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, fourth year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, fourth year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元二九四年）

translations.literal: jiayin, AD 294)
translations.idiomatic: jiayin, AD 294)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁酉，安昌元公石鑒薨。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on dingyou, Yuan Duke Shi Jian of Anchang died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingyou, Yuan Duke Shi Jian of Anchang died.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，匈奴郝散反，攻上黨，殺長吏。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: the Xiongnu Hao San rebelled, attacked Shangdang, and killed the chief official.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, the Xiongnu Hao San rebelled, attacked Shangdang, and killed the chief official.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，郝散帥眾降，馮翊都尉殺之。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: Hao San led his followers in surrender; the Commandant of Fengyi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Hao San led his followers in surrender; the Commandant of Fengyi killed him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大饑。

translations.literal: That year, there was great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year, there was great famine.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉傅咸卒。

translations.literal: Director of the Capital Fu Xian died.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Capital Fu Xian died.

sentences.zh: 咸性剛簡，風格峻整，初為司隸校尉，上言：「貨賂流行，所宜深絕。」

translations.literal: Xian was by nature stern and plain, his conduct sharp and orderly; when he first served as Director of the Capital, he submitted a memorial: "Bribery runs rampant—it ought to be thoroughly abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian was by nature stern and plain, his conduct sharp and orderly; when he first served as Director of the Capital, he submitted a memorial: "Bribery runs rampant—it ought to be thoroughly abolished."

sentences.zh: 時朝政寬弛，權豪放恣，咸奏免河南尹澹等官，京師肅然。

translations.literal: At the time court governance was lax; powerful families acted wildly and without restraint; Xian memorialized to dismiss from office the Administrator of Henan Dan and others—the capital became solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time court governance was lax; powerful families acted wildly and without restraint; Fu Xian memorialized to dismiss from office the Administrator of Henan Dan and others—the capital became solemn and orderly.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆徙居大棘城。

translations.literal: Murong Hui moved his residence to Daji City.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui moved his residence to Daji City.

sentences.zh: 拓跋弗卒，叔父祿官立。

translations.literal: Tuoba Fu died; his uncle Liguan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Fu died; his uncle Liguan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, fifth year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, fifth year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元二九五年）

translations.literal: yimao, AD 295)
translations.idiomatic: yimao, AD 295)

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，東海雨雹，深五寸。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: hail fell in Donghai, five inches deep.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, hail fell in Donghai, five inches deep.

sentences.zh: 荊、揚、兗、豫、青、徐六州大水。

translations.literal: The six provinces of Jing, Yang, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Xu suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The six provinces of Jing, Yang, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Xu suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，武庫火，焚累代之寶及二百萬人器械。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the Arsenal caught fire, burning treasures accumulated over generations and weapons for two million men.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Arsenal caught fire, burning treasures accumulated over generations and weapons for two million men.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，新作武庫，大調兵器。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on bingxu: a new Arsenal was built and weapons were mobilized on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, a new Arsenal was built and weapons were mobilized on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 拓跋祿官分其國為三部：一居上谷之北、濡源之西，自統之；

translations.literal: Tuoba Liguan divided his state into three parts: one part dwelt north of Shanggu and west of the Ruyuan—he ruled this himself;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Liguan divided his state into three parts: one part dwelt north of Shanggu and west of the Ruyuan—he ruled this himself;

sentences.zh: 一居代郡參合陂之北，使兄沙漠汗之子猗□統之；

translations.literal: one dwelt north of Canhe Marsh in Dai Commandery—he had his elder brother Shamo Han's son Yilu rule it;
translations.idiomatic: one dwelt north of Canhe Marsh in Dai Commandery—he had his elder brother Shamo Han's son Yilu rule it;

sentences.zh: 一居定襄之盛樂故城，使猗□弟猗戶統之。

translations.literal: one dwelt at the old city of Shengle in Dingxiang—he had Yilu's younger brother Yihu rule it.
translations.idiomatic: one dwelt at the old city of Shengle in Dingxiang—he had Yilu's younger brother Yihu rule it.

sentences.zh: 猗盧善用兵，西擊匈奴、烏桓諸部，皆破之。

translations.literal: Yilu was skilled in the use of troops; marching west he attacked the Xiongnu and Wuhuan tribes and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu was skilled in the use of troops; marching west he attacked the Xiongnu and Wuhuan tribes and defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 代人衛操與從子雄及同郡箕澹往依拓跋氏，說猗□、猗戶招納晉人。

translations.literal: Dai native Wei Cao, together with his nephew Xiong and fellow townsman Ji Dan, went to rely on the Tuoba clan and urged Yilu and Yihu to recruit and accept Jin people.
translations.idiomatic: Dai native Wei Cao, together with his nephew Xiong and fellow townsman Ji Dan, went to rely on the Tuoba clan and urged Yilu and Yihu to recruit and accept Jin people.

sentences.zh: 猗□悅之，任以國事，晉人附者稍眾。

translations.literal: Yilu was pleased and entrusted them with state affairs; Jin people who attached themselves gradually grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu was pleased and entrusted them with state affairs; Jin people who attached themselves gradually grew numerous.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, sixth year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, sixth year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元二九六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, AD 296)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, AD 296)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，赦天下。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: a general amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, a general amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 下邳獻王晃薨。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Xiapi, Huang, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Xiapi, Huang, died.

sentences.zh: 以中書監張華為司空。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太尉隴西王泰行尚書令，徙封高密王。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince Tai of Longxi acted as Director of the Department of State Affairs and was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Prince Tai of Longxi acted as Director of the Department of State Affairs and was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 夏，郝散弟度元與馮翊、北地馬蘭羌、盧水胡俱反，殺北地太守張損，敗馮翊太守歐陽建。

translations.literal: Summer: Hao San's younger brother Duyuan rebelled together with the Malan Qiang of Fengyi and Beidi and the Lushui Hu, killing Administrator of Beidi Zhang Sun and defeating Administrator of Fengyi Ouyang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, Hao San's younger brother Duyuan rebelled together with the Malan Qiang of Fengyi and Beidi and the Lushui Hu, killing Administrator of Beidi Zhang Sun and defeating Administrator of Fengyi Ouyang Jian.

sentences.zh: 征西大將軍趙王倫信用嬖人琅邪孫秀，與雍州刺史濟南解係爭軍事，更相表奏，歐陽建亦表倫罪惡。

translations.literal: Grand General Conquering the West Prince Lun of Zhao trusted his favorite Langya Sun Xiu; he quarreled with Yong Province Inspector Jie Xi of Jinan over military affairs, each repeatedly memorializing against the other, and Ouyang Jian also memorialized against Lun's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Conquering the West Prince Lun of Zhao trusted his favorite Langya Sun Xiu; he quarreled with Yong Province Inspector Jie Xi of Jinan over military affairs, each repeatedly memorializing against the other, and Ouyang Jian also memorialized against Prince Lun's crimes.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以倫撓亂關右，征倫為車騎將軍，以梁王肜為征西大將軍、都督雍、涼二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: The court, because Lun was disrupting the region west of the passes, summoned Lun as Chariot-and-Cavalry General and appointed Prince Rong of Liang as Grand General Conquering the West, Commander over all military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The court, because Prince Lun was disrupting the region west of the passes, summoned him as Chariot-and-Cavalry General and appointed Prince Rong of Liang as Grand General Conquering the West, Commander over all military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.

sentences.zh: 系與其弟御史中丞結，皆表請誅秀以謝氐、羌；

translations.literal: Jie Xi and his younger brother, Imperial Censor Attendant-in-Chief Jie, both memorialized requesting the execution of Sun Xiu to appease the Di and Qiang;
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xi and his younger brother, Imperial Censor Attendant-in-Chief Jie, both memorialized requesting the execution of Sun Xiu to appease the Di and Qiang;

sentences.zh: 張華以告梁王肜，使誅之，肜許諾。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua reported this to Prince Rong of Liang and had him execute Xiu; Rong promised to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua reported this to Prince Rong of Liang and had him execute Sun Xiu; Prince Rong promised to do so.

sentences.zh: 秀友人辛冉為之說肜曰：「氐、羌自反，非秀之罪。」

translations.literal: Sun Xiu's friend Xin Ran spoke on his behalf to Rong, saying, "The Di and Qiang rebelled on their own—this is not Xiu's crime."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's friend Xin Ran spoke on his behalf to Prince Rong of Liang, saying, "The Di and Qiang rebelled on their own—this is not Sun Xiu's crime."

sentences.zh: 秀由是得免。

translations.literal: Xiu was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 倫至洛陽，用秀計，深交賈、郭，賈後大愛信之，倫因求錄尚書事，又求尚書令；

translations.literal: When Lun reached Luoyang, using Xiu's plan he cultivated deep ties with the Jia and Guo families; Empress Jia came to love and trust him greatly; Lun thereupon requested appointment as Recorder of Affairs for the Department of State Affairs, and further requested the directorship of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lun reached Luoyang, using Sun Xiu's plan he cultivated deep ties with the Jia and Guo families; Empress Jia came to love and trust him greatly; Prince Lun thereupon requested appointment as Recorder of Affairs for the Department of State Affairs, and further requested the directorship of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 張華、裴頠固執以為不可，倫、秀由是怨之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua and Pei Ji steadfastly maintained it was impossible; Lun and Xiu therefore resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Pei Ji steadfastly maintained it was impossible; Prince Lun and Sun Xiu therefore resented them.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，解系為郝度元所敗，秦雍氐、羌悉後，立氐帥齊萬年為帝，圍涇陽。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: Jie Xi was defeated by Hao Duyuan; the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong rebelled one after another, set up the Di chieftain Qi Wannian as emperor, and besieged Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Jie Xi was defeated by Hao Duyuan; the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong rebelled one after another, set up the Di chieftain Qi Wannian as emperor, and besieged Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞周處，彈劾不避權戚，梁王肜嘗違法，處按劾之。

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Attendant-in-Chief Zhou Chu, when impeaching, did not avoid powerful kin; Prince Rong of Liang had once violated the law, and Chu impeached him accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Censor Attendant-in-Chief Zhou Chu, when impeaching, did not avoid powerful kin; Prince Rong of Liang had once violated the law, and Zhou Chu impeached him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，詔以處為建威將軍，與振威將軍盧播俱隸安西將軍夏侯駿，以討齊萬年。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: an edict appointed Chu as General Establishing Might and Lu Bo as General Quelling Might, both under Anxi General Xiahou Jun, to campaign against Qi Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, an edict appointed Zhou Chu as General Establishing Might and Lu Bo as General Quelling Might, both under Anxi General Xiahou Jun, to campaign against Qi Wannian.

sentences.zh: 中書令陳准言於朝曰：「駿及梁王皆貴戚，非將帥之才，進不求名，退不畏罪。

translations.literal: Secretary Supervisor Chen Zhun said at court: "Jun and the Prince of Liang are both imperial kin—they are not talents for command; advancing they seek no fame, retreating they fear no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Supervisor Chen Zhun said at court: "Xiahou Jun and the Prince of Liang are both imperial kin—they are not talents for command; advancing they seek no fame, retreating they fear no punishment.

sentences.zh: 周處吳人，忠直勇果，有仇無援。

translations.literal: Zhou Chu is a man of Wu—loyal, upright, brave, and resolute; he has enemies and no backers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu is a man of Wu—loyal, upright, brave, and resolute; he has enemies and no backers.

sentences.zh: 宜詔積弩將軍孟觀，以精兵萬人為處前鋒，必能殄寇；

translations.literal: It would be fitting to decree that Repeated-Bow General Meng Guan, with ten thousand elite troops, serve as Chu's vanguard—they will surely be able to exterminate the bandits;
translations.idiomatic: It would be fitting to decree that Repeated-Bow General Meng Guan, with ten thousand elite troops, serve as Zhou Chu's vanguard—they will surely be able to exterminate the bandits;

sentences.zh: 不然，梁王當使處先驅，以不救陷而之，其敗必也。」

translations.literal: otherwise the Prince of Liang will use Chu as vanguard and, failing to rescue him, let him fall into disaster—defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the Prince of Liang will use Zhou Chu as vanguard and, failing to rescue him, let him fall into disaster—defeat is certain."

sentences.zh: 朝廷不從。

translations.literal: The court did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 齊萬年聞處來，曰：「周府君嘗為新平太守，有文武才，若專斷而來，不可當也；

translations.literal: When Qi Wannian heard Chu was coming, he said, "Prefect Zhou once served as Administrator of Xinping—he has both civil and military talent; if he comes acting on independent authority, he cannot be withstood;
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wannian heard Zhou Chu was coming, he said, "Prefect Zhou once served as Administrator of Xinping—he has both civil and military talent; if he comes acting on independent authority, he cannot be withstood;

sentences.zh: 或受制於人，此成禽耳！」

translations.literal: or if he is constrained by others, he will easily be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: or if he is constrained by others, he will easily be captured!"

sentences.zh: 關中饑、疫。

translations.literal: Within the passes there were famine and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Within the passes there were famine and pestilence.

sentences.zh: 初，略陽清水氐楊駒始居仇池。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Ju of the Qingshui Di of Lüeyang first settled at Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Ju of the Qingshui Di of Lüeyang first settled at Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 仇池方百傾，其旁平地二十餘里，四面斗絕而高，為羊腸蟠道三十六回而上。

translations.literal: Qiuchi covered a hundred qing in area; level ground beside it extended more than twenty li; on all sides it rose steep and isolated; a twisting goat-path of thirty-six switchbacks led upward.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuchi covered a hundred qing in area; level ground beside it extended more than twenty li; on all sides it rose steep and isolated; a twisting goat-path of thirty-six switchbacks led upward.

sentences.zh: 至其孫千萬附魏，封為百頃王。

translations.literal: When it reached his grandson Qianwan, he submitted to Wei and was enfeoffed as Prince of the Hundred Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to his grandson Qianwan, he submitted to Wei and was enfeoffed as Prince of the Hundred Qing.

sentences.zh: 千萬孫飛龍浸強盛，徙居略陽。

translations.literal: Qianwan's grandson Feilong gradually grew powerful and moved to settle at Lüeyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwan's grandson Feilong gradually grew powerful and moved to settle at Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 飛龍以其甥令狐茂搜為子，茂搜避齊萬年之亂，十二月，自略陽帥部落四千家還保仇池，自號輔國將軍、右賢王。

translations.literal: Feilong took his nephew Linghu Maosou as his adopted son. Maosou, fleeing the turmoil of Qi Wannian's rebellion, in the twelfth month led four thousand families of his tribe from Lüeyang back to hold Qiuchi, styling himself General Who Supports the State and Right Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Feilong took his nephew Linghu Maosou as his adopted son. To escape the turmoil of Qi Wannian's rebellion, in the twelfth month Maosou led four thousand families of his tribe from Lüeyang back to hold Qiuchi, styling himself General Who Supports the State and Right Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 關中人士避亂者多依之，茂搜迎接撫納，欲去者，衛護資送之。

translations.literal: Many people of the Guanzhong region fleeing disorder relied on him; Maosou received, comforted, and accepted them; those who wished to leave, he guarded, escorted, and provided for their departure.
translations.idiomatic: Many people of the Guanzhong region fleeing disorder relied on him; Maosou received them, comforted them, and took them in; those who wished to leave he guarded, escorted, and provided for their departure.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以揚烈將軍巴西趙廞為益州刺史，發梁、益兵糧助雍州討氐、羌。

translations.literal: That year, General Who Displays Martial Majesty Zhao Yin of Baxi was made Inspector of Yizhou; troops and provisions from Liang and Yizhou were mobilized to assist Yong Province in campaigning against the Di and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, General Who Displays Martial Majesty Zhao Yin of Baxi was made Inspector of Yizhou, and troops and provisions from Liang and Yizhou were mobilized to assist Yong Province in campaigning against the Di and Qiang.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之上元康七年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, first part, upper, seventh year of Yuankang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, first part, upper section, seventh year of Yuankang (

sentences.zh: 丁巳、公元二九七年）

translations.literal: dingsi, AD 297)
translations.idiomatic: dingsi, AD 297)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，齊萬年屯梁山，有眾七萬；

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Qi Wannian encamped at Liang Mountain with a force of seventy thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Qi Wannian encamped at Liang Mountain with a force of seventy thousand;

sentences.zh: 梁王肜、夏侯駿使周處以五千兵擊之。

translations.literal: the Prince of Liang Rong and Xiahou Jun sent Zhou Chu with five thousand troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Liang Rong and Xiahou Jun sent Zhou Chu with five thousand troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 處曰：「軍無後繼，必敗，不徒亡身，為國取恥。」

translations.literal: Chu said, "The army has no reserve—it will certainly be defeated; not only will I lose my life in vain, I will bring disgrace upon the state."
translations.idiomatic: Chu said, "The army has no reserve—it will certainly be defeated; I will not merely lose my life in vain but bring disgrace upon the state."

sentences.zh: 肜、駿不聽，逼遣之。

translations.literal: Rong and Jun would not listen and compelled him to go.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Jun would not listen and compelled him to go.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，處與盧播、解系攻萬年於六陌。

translations.literal: On guichou day, Chu together with Lu Bo and Xie Xi attacked Wannian at Liumo.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day, Chu together with Lu Bo and Xie Xi attacked Wannian at Liumo.

sentences.zh: 處軍士未食，肜促令速進，自旦戰至暮，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Chu's troops had not eaten; Rong pressed for a rapid advance; from morning until evening they fought, killing and capturing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's troops had not eaten, but Rong pressed for a rapid advance; from morning until evening they fought, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 弦絕矢盡，救兵不至。

translations.literal: Bowstrings snapped and arrows were exhausted; reinforcements did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Bowstrings snapped and arrows were exhausted, and reinforcements did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 左右勸處退，處按劍曰：「是吾效節致命之日也！」

translations.literal: Those beside him urged Chu to withdraw; he grasped his sword and said, "This is the day on which I fulfill my duty and give my life!"
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him urged Chu to withdraw; he grasped his sword and said, "This is the day on which I fulfill my duty and give my life!"

sentences.zh: 遂力戰而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖以尤肜，而亦不能罪也。

translations.literal: Although the court blamed Rong for this, it could not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Although the court blamed Rong for this, it could not punish him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，雍、秦二州大旱，疾疫，米斛萬錢。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Yong and Qin provinces suffered great drought and pestilence; grain was ten thousand cash per hu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yong and Qin provinces suffered great drought and pestilence; grain cost ten thousand cash per hu.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，京陵元公王渾薨。

translations.literal: On dingchou day, Wang Hun, Duke Yuan of Jingling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, Wang Hun, Duke Yuan of Jingling, died.

sentences.zh: 九月，以尚書右僕射王戎為司徒，太子太師何劭為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Rong was made Minister over the Masses; Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Rong was made Minister over the Masses, and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 戎為三公，與時浮沉，無所匡救，委事僚寀，輕出遊放。

translations.literal: As one of the Three Dukes, Rong drifted with the times, offering no correction or rescue; he delegated affairs to his clerks and attendants and went out lightly for pleasure and wandering.
translations.idiomatic: As one of the Three Dukes, Rong drifted with the times, offering no correction or rescue; he delegated affairs to his clerks and attendants and went out lightly for pleasure and wandering.

sentences.zh: 性復貪吝，園田遍天下，每自執牙籌，晝夜會計，常若不足。

translations.literal: By nature he was also greedy and stingy; his gardens and fields spread throughout the empire; he personally wielded counting sticks day and night reckoning accounts, always as though he lacked enough.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was also greedy and stingy; his gardens and fields spread throughout the empire; he personally wielded counting sticks day and night reckoning accounts, always as though he never had enough.

sentences.zh: 家有好李，賣之恐人得種，常鑽其核。

translations.literal: His household had fine plums; fearing that if he sold them others might obtain the seeds, he regularly bored holes through the pits.
translations.idiomatic: His household had fine plums; fearing that if he sold them others might obtain the seeds, he regularly bored holes through the pits.

sentences.zh: 凡所賞拔，專事虛名。

translations.literal: All those he rewarded and promoted he did solely for empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: All those he rewarded and promoted he did solely for empty reputation.

sentences.zh: 阮咸之子瞻嘗見戎，戎問曰：「聖人貴名教，老、莊明自然，其旨同異？」

translations.literal: Ruan Xian's son Zhan once visited Rong; Rong asked, "The sages honor name and teaching; Laozi and Zhuangzi clarify naturalness—are their purports the same or different?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian's son Zhan once visited Rong; Rong asked, "The sages honor name and teaching; Laozi and Zhuangzi clarify naturalness—are their purports the same or different?"

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「將無同！」

translations.literal: Zhan said, "Perhaps they are not different!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "Perhaps they are not different!"

sentences.zh: 戎咨嗟良久，遂辟之。

translations.literal: Rong sighed in admiration for a long while and then recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sighed in admiration for a long while and then recruited him.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之「三語掾」。

translations.literal: People of the time called him "the Three-Phrase Staff Officer."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him "the Three-Phrase Staff Officer."

sentences.zh: 是時，王衍為尚書令，南陽樂廣為河南尹，皆善清談，宅心事外，名重當世，朝野之人，爭慕效之。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Yan was Secretary Supervisor and Yue Guang of Nanyang was Intendant of Henan; both were skilled in pure discourse, dwelling in the heart on matters beyond the world; their fame weighed heavily in the age; men of court and country competed to admire and imitate them.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Yan was Secretary Supervisor and Yue Guang of Nanyang was Intendant of Henan; both were skilled in pure discourse and dwelt in the heart on matters beyond the world; their fame weighed heavily in the age, and men of court and country competed to admire and imitate them.

sentences.zh: 衍與弟澄，好題品人物，舉世以為儀准。

translations.literal: Yan and his younger brother Cheng loved to appraise and rank people; all the world took them as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his younger brother Cheng loved to appraise and rank people; all the world took them as the standard.

sentences.zh: 衍神情明秀，少時，山濤見之，嗟歎良久，曰：「何物老嫗，生寧馨兒！

translations.literal: Yan's spirit and expression were bright and refined; when young, Shan Tao saw him, sighed in admiration for a long while, and said, "What sort of old woman bore such a fine son!
translations.idiomatic: Yan's spirit and expression were bright and refined; when young, Shan Tao saw him, sighed in admiration for a long while, and said, "What sort of old woman bore such a fine son!

sentences.zh: 然誤天下蒼生者，未必非此人也！」

translations.literal: Yet the one who may mislead the myriad people under Heaven is perhaps none other than this man!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the one who may mislead the myriad people under Heaven is perhaps none other than this man!"

sentences.zh: 樂廣性沖約清遠，與物無競。

translations.literal: Yue Guang's nature was mild, restrained, pure, and far-reaching; he did not contend with things.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang's nature was mild, restrained, pure, and far-reaching; he did not contend with things.

sentences.zh: 每談論，以約言析理，厭人之心，而其所不知，默如也。

translations.literal: Whenever he discoursed, with brief words he analyzed principle and satisfied people's minds; what he did not know, he was silent as though it were nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he discoursed, with brief words he analyzed principle and satisfied people's minds; what he did not know, he remained silent as though it were nothing.

sentences.zh: 凡論人，必先稱其所長，則所短不言自見。

translations.literal: Whenever he judged men, he always first praised their strengths; then their weaknesses became visible without his saying them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he judged men, he always first praised their strengths; then their weaknesses became visible without his saying them.

sentences.zh: 王澄及阮咸、咸從子修、泰山胡毋輔之、陳國謝鯤、城陽王夷、新蔡畢卓，皆以任放為達，至於醉狂裸體，不以為非。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng, Ruan Xian, Xian's nephew Xiu, Huwu Zhi of Taishan, Xie Kun of Chen, Prince of Chengyang Yi, and Bi Zhuo of Xincai all took reckless indulgence for transcendence—going so far as drunkenness, madness, and nakedness—and did not regard it as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, Ruan Xian, Xian's nephew Xiu, Huwu Zhi of Taishan, Xie Kun of Chen, Prince of Chengyang Yi, and Bi Zhuo of Xincai all took reckless indulgence for transcendence—going so far as drunkenness, madness, and nakedness—and did not regard it as wrong.

sentences.zh: 胡毋輔之嘗酣飲，其子謙之窺而厲聲呼其父字曰：「彥國！

translations.literal: Huwu Zhi was once drinking deeply; his son Qianzhi peeped in and in a stern voice called his father's courtesy name: "Yan'guo!
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Zhi was once drinking deeply; his son Qianzhi peeped in and in a stern voice called his father's courtesy name: "Yan'guo!

sentences.zh: 年老，不得為爾！」

translations.literal: You are old—you must not behave like this!"
translations.idiomatic: You are old—you must not behave like this!"

sentences.zh: 輔之歡笑，呼入共飲。

translations.literal: Zhi laughed with delight and called him in to drink together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi laughed with delight and called him in to drink together.

sentences.zh: 畢卓嘗為吏部郎，比捨郎釀熟，卓因醉，夜至甕間盜飲之，為掌酒者所縛，明旦視之，乃畢吏部也。

translations.literal: Bi Zhuo had once been Director of the Ministry of Official Personnel; when a neighboring Gentleman of Lang's brew matured, Zhuo, being drunk, went at night to the vats and stole drink; the wine steward bound him, and at dawn when they looked, it turned out to be Director Bi of the Ministry of Official Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhuo had once been Director of the Ministry of Official Personnel; when a neighboring Gentleman of Lang's brew matured, Zhuo, being drunk, went at night to the vats and stole drink; the wine steward bound him, and at dawn when they looked, it turned out to be Director Bi of the Ministry of Official Personnel.

sentences.zh: 樂廣聞而笑之，曰：「名教內自有樂地，何必乃爾！」

translations.literal: Yue Guang heard and laughed at this, saying, "Within name and teaching there is joy enough—why must one go to such lengths!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang heard and laughed at this, saying, "Within name and teaching there is joy enough—why must one go to such lengths!"

sentences.zh: 初，何晏等祖述老、莊，立論以為：「天地萬物，皆以無為本。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Yan and others traced back to Laozi and Zhuangzi and established a doctrine holding: "Heaven, earth, and the myriad things all take nonbeing as their root.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, He Yan and others traced back to Laozi and Zhuangzi and established a doctrine holding: "Heaven, earth, and the myriad things all take nonbeing as their root.

sentences.zh: 無也者，開物成務，無往不存者也。

translations.literal: Nonbeing is that which opens things and accomplishes tasks, that which exists wherever one goes.
translations.idiomatic: Nonbeing is that which opens things and accomplishes tasks, that which exists wherever one goes.

sentences.zh: 陰陽恃以化生，賢者恃以成德。

translations.literal: Yin and yang rely on it to produce and transform; the worthy rely on it to complete virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang rely on it to produce and transform; the worthy rely on it to complete virtue.

sentences.zh: 故無之為用，無爵而貴矣！」

translations.literal: Therefore the use of nonbeing is honored though it has no rank!"
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the use of nonbeing is honored though it has no rank!"

sentences.zh: 王衍之徒皆愛重之。

translations.literal: Wang Yan and his followers all prized and honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and his followers all prized and honored this.

sentences.zh: 由是朝廷士大夫皆以浮誕為美，弛廢職業。

translations.literal: From this, the scholar-officials of the court all took empty extravagance for beauty and slackened and abandoned their duties.
translations.idiomatic: From this, the scholar-officials of the court all took empty extravagance for beauty and slackened and abandoned their duties.

sentences.zh: 裴頠著《崇有論》以釋其蔽曰：「夫利慾可損，而未可絕有也；

translations.literal: Pei Ji wrote 《On Honoring Being》 to clarify this delusion, saying: "Desire for profit can be reduced, yet one cannot utterly deny being;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji wrote 《On Honoring Being》 to clarify this delusion, saying: "Desire for profit can be reduced, yet one cannot utterly deny being;

sentences.zh: 事務可節，而未可全無也。

translations.literal: affairs can be restrained, yet one cannot do altogether without them.
translations.idiomatic: affairs can be restrained, yet one cannot do altogether without them.

sentences.zh: 蓋有飾為高談之具者，深列有形之累，盛稱空無之美。

translations.literal: Presumably there are those who dress up empty talk as their instrument, deeply enumerating the burdens of having form and greatly praising the beauty of empty nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: Presumably there are those who dress up empty talk as their instrument, deeply enumerating the burdens of having form and greatly praising the beauty of empty nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 形器之累有征，空無之義難檢；

translations.literal: The burdens of form and implements have manifest signs; the doctrine of empty nonbeing is hard to verify;
translations.idiomatic: The burdens of form and implements have manifest signs; the doctrine of empty nonbeing is hard to verify;

sentences.zh: 辯巧之文可悅，似象之言足惑。

translations.literal: artful argumentative prose can please; language resembling truth can fully beguile.
translations.idiomatic: artful argumentative prose can please; language resembling truth can fully beguile.

sentences.zh: 眾聽眩焉，溺其成說。

translations.literal: The multitude's hearing is dazzled, and they drown in this established doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude's hearing is dazzled, and they drown in this established doctrine.

sentences.zh: 雖頗有異此心者，辭不獲濟，屈於所習，因謂虛無之理誠不可蓋。

translations.literal: Though some differed in mind, their words could not prevail; yielding to what they had learned, they thus held that the principle of emptiness and nonbeing truly could not be surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Though some differed in mind, their words could not prevail; yielding to what they had learned, they thus held that the principle of emptiness and nonbeing truly could not be surpassed.

sentences.zh: 一唱百和，往而不反，遂薄綜世之務，賤功利之用，高浮游之業，卑經實之賢。

translations.literal: One voice sang and a hundred harmonized; they went forth and did not return—thereupon they slighted affairs that ordered the age, despised the use of profit and utility, exalted the pursuit of idle wandering, and debased the worthy who upheld the classics and reality.
translations.idiomatic: One voice sang and a hundred harmonized; they went forth and did not return—thereupon they slighted affairs that ordered the age, despised the use of profit and utility, exalted the pursuit of idle wandering, and debased the worthy who upheld the classics and reality.

sentences.zh: 人情所徇，名利從之，於是文者衍其辭，訥者贊其旨。

translations.literal: As human feelings were indulged, fame and profit followed; thus the eloquent elaborated their phrasing, and the inarticulate praised their purport.
translations.idiomatic: As human feelings were indulged, fame and profit followed; thus the eloquent elaborated their phrasing, and the inarticulate praised their purport.

sentences.zh: 立言藉於虛無，謂之玄妙；

translations.literal: Setting forth words relying on emptiness and nonbeing, they called it profound mystery;
translations.idiomatic: Setting forth words relying on emptiness and nonbeing, they called it profound mystery;

sentences.zh: 處官不親所職，謂之雅遠；

translations.literal: holding office without attending to one's duties, they called it elegant distance;
translations.idiomatic: holding office without attending to one's duties, they called it elegant distance;

sentences.zh: 奉身散其廉操，謂之曠達。

translations.literal: squandering one's integrity and scruples, they called it free and transcendent.
translations.idiomatic: squandering one's integrity and scruples, they called it free and transcendent.

sentences.zh: 故砥礪之風，彌以陵遲。

translations.literal: Therefore the spirit of tempering and grinding grew daily more decadent.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the spirit of tempering and grinding grew daily more decadent.

sentences.zh: 放者因斯，或悖吉凶之禮，忽容止之表，瀆長幼之序，混貴賤之級，甚者至於裸裎褻慢，無所不至，士行又虧矣。

translations.literal: The indulgent seized on this—some violated rites of auspice and misfortune, neglected the outward forms of deportment, profaned the order of elders and juniors, mixed noble and base ranks; in extreme cases they went so far as naked exposure and shameless contempt, reaching to everything imaginable—and conduct among gentlemen was further debased.
translations.idiomatic: The indulgent seized on this—some violated rites of auspice and misfortune, neglected the outward forms of deportment, profaned the order of elders and juniors, and mixed noble and base ranks; in extreme cases they went so far as naked exposure and shameless contempt, reaching to everything imaginable—and conduct among gentlemen was further debased.

sentences.zh: 「夫萬物之有形者，雖生於無，然生以有為已分，則無是有之所遺者也。

translations.literal: "Among the myriad things, those that have form, though born from nonbeing, yet once born take being as their allotted portion—nonbeing is therefore what being leaves behind.
translations.idiomatic: "Among the myriad things, those that have form, though born from nonbeing, yet once born take being as their allotted portion—nonbeing is therefore what being leaves behind.

sentences.zh: 故養既化之有，非無用之所能全也；

translations.literal: Therefore nurturing what has already transformed into being is not something that useless nonaction can fully accomplish;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore nurturing what has already transformed into being is not something that useless nonaction can fully accomplish;

sentences.zh: 治既有之眾，非無為之所能修也。

translations.literal: governing the multitude that already exists is not something that nonaction can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: governing the multitude that already exists is not something that nonaction can accomplish.

sentences.zh: 心非事也，而制事必由於心，然不可謂心為無也；

translations.literal: The mind is not an affair, yet governing affairs must proceed through the mind—yet one cannot call the mind nonbeing;
translations.idiomatic: The mind is not an affair, yet governing affairs must proceed through the mind—yet one cannot call the mind nonbeing;

sentences.zh: 匠非器也，而制器必須於匠，然不可謂匠非有也。

translations.literal: The craftsman is not the vessel, yet making vessels must depend on the craftsman—yet one cannot say the craftsman is not being.
translations.idiomatic: The craftsman is not the vessel, yet making vessels must depend on the craftsman—yet one cannot say the craftsman is not being.

sentences.zh: 是以欲收重淵之鱗，非偃息之所能獲也；

translations.literal: Therefore to gather the scaled creatures of the deep abyss is not something that lying down to rest can obtain;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to gather the scaled creatures of the deep abyss is not something that lying down to rest can obtain;

sentences.zh: 隕高墉之禽，非靜拱之所能捷也。

translations.literal: to bring down the birds of a high wall is not something that sitting still with folded hands can capture.
translations.idiomatic: to bring down the birds of a high wall is not something that sitting still with folded hands can capture.

sentences.zh: 由此而觀，濟有者皆有也，虛無奚益於已有之群生哉！」

translations.literal: Viewed from this, those who aid being all rely on being—what good does emptiness and nonbeing do for living beings that already exist!"
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, those who aid being all rely on being—what good does emptiness and nonbeing do for living beings that already exist!"

sentences.zh: 然習俗已成，頠論亦不能救也。

translations.literal: Yet the custom was already formed, and Ji's treatise could not save it either.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the custom was already formed, and Ji's treatise could not save it either.

sentences.zh: 拓跋猗迤度漠北巡，因西略諸國，積五歲，降附者三十餘國。

translations.literal: Tuoba Yitu crossed the desert northward on patrol and thereby marched west to subdue the various states; over five years, more than thirty states submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Yitu crossed the desert northward on patrol and thereby marched west to subdue the various states; over five years, more than thirty states submitted.

translations.literal: Spring, third month, on renxu day, a general amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, on renxu day, a general amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，荊、豫、徐、揚、冀五州大水。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: Jing, Yu, Xu, Yang, and Ji provinces suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, Jing, Yu, Xu, Yang, and Ji provinces suffered great floods.

translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Lu was in Hanzhong, the Li clan of the Cong people from Dangqu in Baxi went to rely on him.

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei took Hanzhong, the Li clan led more than five hundred families to submit; they were appointed generals and moved to the northern lands of Lüeyang, styled the Ba Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei took Hanzhong, the Li clan led more than five hundred families to submit; they were appointed generals and moved to the northern lands of Lüeyang, styled the Ba Di.

sentences.zh: 其孫特，庠、流，皆有材武，善騎射，性任俠，州黨多附之。

translations.literal: His grandsons Te, Xiang, and Liu all had talent and martial prowess, were skilled in horsemanship and archery, and by nature were chivalrous and daring; many in the district attached themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Te, Xiang, and Liu all had talent and martial prowess, were skilled in horsemanship and archery, and by nature were chivalrous and daring; many in the district attached themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 及齊萬年反，關中荐饑，略陽、天水等六郡民流移就谷入漢川者數萬家，道路有疾病窮乏者，特兄弟常營護振救之，由是得眾心。

translations.literal: When Qi Wannian rebelled, famine recurred in Guanzhong; tens of thousands of families from the six commanderies of Lüeyang, Tianshui, and others flowed away seeking grain and entered Hanchuan; on the roads there were the sick and destitute—the Te brothers regularly cared for, protected, and relieved them, and thereby won the people's hearts.

translations.literal: The court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

translations.literal: Thereupon they scattered through Liang and Yi and could not be prevented.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they scattered through Liang and Yi and could not be prevented.

sentences.zh: 李特至劍閣，太息曰：「劉禪有如此地，面縛於人，豈非庸才邪！」

translations.literal: When Li Te reached Jian'ge Pass, he sighed deeply and said, "Liu Shan had terrain such as this, yet he bound himself and surrendered to another—is he not a mediocrity!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Te reached Jian'ge Pass, he sighed deeply and said, "Liu Shan had terrain such as this, yet he bound himself and surrendered to another—is he not a mediocrity!"

sentences.zh: 聞者異之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were startled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were startled.

sentences.zh: 張華、陳准以趙王、梁王，相繼在關中，皆雍容驕貴，師老無功，乃薦孟觀沉毅有文武材用，使討齊萬年。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua and Chen Zhun, because the Prince of Zhao and the Prince of Liang had successively been in Guanzhong—both easy and grand, proud and noble, with troops weary and without achievement—thereupon recommended Meng Guan as deep, resolute, and possessed of civil and military talent, and had him campaign against Qi Wannian.

sentences.zh: 觀身當矢石，大戰十數，皆破之。

translations.literal: Guan personally exposed himself to arrows and stones, fought more than ten great battles, and broke the enemy each time.
